urgent_if: severe pain in the upper abdomen or right side lasting more than a few hours
fever with chills or jaundice
persistent vomiting or inability to keep fluids down
pain spreading to the back or right shoulder

about.reply: Gallstones are hard deposits that form in your gallbladder, a small pear-shaped organ under the liver that stores bile to help digest fat. They form when substances in bile harden and can block the bile duct, which often causes pain in the abdomen, back or under the right arm, sometimes with nausea or vomiting after eating.
about.next_step: See a doctor promptly if you have sudden upper abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting after meals, or pain that spreads to the back or right shoulder.
about.why: Gallstones are common in older adults, women, overweight people and some ethnic groups, and are often found incidentally on imaging. If you have no symptoms, treatment is usually not needed; if you have attacks, a doctor will decide if treatment is needed.

care.reply: You can try reducing swallowed air and food-related gas now by drinking water and non-fizzy drinks, eating more slowly, and avoiding milk products if lactose intolerance is suspected.
care.next_step: Try these measures for a few days and note which foods make it worse; see a health care provider if the gas, bloating or pain still bothers you.
care.why: Gas comes from swallowed air and breakdown of undigested food by bacteria in the large intestine, and certain foods cause gas in some people but not others. Medicines can help with gas or pain, but a provider should guide use.

about.reply: Gas is air you swallow and gas made when bacteria in the large intestine break down undigested food.
about.why: Gas comes from swallowed air and bacterial breakdown of food, and odor comes from sulfur gases made by bacteria. Certain foods cause gas in some people but not others.

care.reply: Gout is a type of inflammatory arthritis caused by uric acid crystals that can build up in joints and cause painful, red, swollen flares, often starting in the big toe or lower limb. For now keep the affected joint rested, cool and elevated, and avoid alcohol and foods high in purines until you can be assessed.
care.next_step: Book a doctor visit within 2 to 3 days for a first flare or if pain and swelling are not clearly improving, and seek care sooner if this is the first episode.
care.why: Flares usually last a week or two and then ease, but a clinician needs to confirm gout and rule out infection or other causes like pseudogout. What helps and what to avoid is individual, so a doctor’s plan comes first.
urgent_if: fever with a hot red joint
unable to bear weight or move the joint
rapidly worsening swelling or skin breaks
signs of infection elsewhere

about.reply: Gout is a type of inflammatory arthritis that causes sudden pain, swelling and redness in one or more joints, often starting in the big toe or lower limb. It happens when uric acid builds up in the blood over time and forms needle-like crystals in a joint, which triggers a flare that usually lasts a week or two.
about.next_step: See a doctor within 2 to 3 days for a painful, red, swollen joint, or sooner if the flare is not improving, is in a new joint, or you have fever.
about.why: Too much uric acid can come from the body making too much or not removing enough, often linked to diet high in purines and other factors. Hyperuricemia does not always cause gout, and only some people form crystals.

about.reply: HDL is high-density lipoprotein, often called 'good' cholesterol because it carries cholesterol from other parts of your body back to your liver so your liver can remove it.
about.next_step: Ask your doctor when you should have a cholesterol blood test based on your age, risk factors and family history.
about.why: HDL moves cholesterol out of arteries, while LDL can build up in arteries. The evidence describes what HDL is and how it is measured, but does not list causes of HDL levels.

care.reply: Hay fever is a pollen allergy that can cause sneezing, runny or clogged nose, itchy eyes, nose and throat, cough and postnasal drip. At home you can try reducing pollen exposure, rinsing the nose with distilled or sterilized saline water, and using over-the-counter symptom relief as directed on the label.
care.next_step: If symptoms are bothersome or not improving with simple measures, book a check with a doctor within 2 to 3 days.
care.why: Pollen in the nose and throat triggers allergy symptoms, and nasal rinses and medicines can relieve them. A doctor can confirm hay fever and discuss longer-term options like allergy shots if needed.

about.reply: Hay fever is an allergy to pollen that irritates the nose and throat. It is commonly caused by pollen from trees, weeds and grasses released in spring, summer and fall that gets into your nose and throat.
about.next_step: See a doctor if symptoms are frequent, bothering daily life, or not easing with simple measures.
about.why: Pollen exposure triggers sneezing, runny or clogged nose, itchy eyes and cough. A provider can confirm it by exam and sometimes skin or blood tests.

care.reply: Call 112 now. For a head injury at home, keep the person safe, rest and watch closely for warning signs, and get medical care promptly if any red flags appear.
care.next_step: Check the person now for the warning signs below and seek a doctor today for any head injury with loss of consciousness, worsening headache, repeated vomiting, confusion, weakness, slurred speech, unequal pupils, seizure, or inability to wake up.
care.why: The skull protects the brain but closed injuries can still be serious, and doctors use a neurologic exam and imaging to assess severity. Warning signs suggest a moderate or severe injury that needs urgent evaluation.
urgent_if: Headache that gets worse or does not go away
Repeated vomiting or nausea
Convulsions or seizures
Inability to wake up

about.reply: A head injury is damage to the skull or brain from a bump, blow or jolt. It can be closed, where the skull is not broken, or open/penetrating where an object goes into the skull. Common causes are falls, motor vehicle accidents, violence and sports injuries.
about.next_step: Get medical care the same day if you have a worsening headache, repeated vomiting, confusion, weakness or numbness, slurred speech, loss of coordination, seizures, inability to wake up, or one pupil larger than the other.
about.why: The skull protects the brain, but injuries can still be moderate or severe even without a break. Doctors use a neurologic exam and imaging to assess severity and decide treatment.
urgent_if: headache that gets worse or does not go away
repeated vomiting or nausea
convulsions or seizures
inability to wake up

care.reply: Head lice are tiny crawling insects that live on the scalp and feed on human blood. They spread mainly by close head-to-head contact, not by poor hygiene, and they do not spread disease. Treatment is usually done with a medicated shampoo or lotion used as directed, plus careful removal of nits and avoiding sharing hats, combs or hairbrushes.
care.next_step: Check the scalp for lice and nits, especially at the neckline and behind the ears, and talk to a pharmacist or doctor today for the right treatment option for your family and how to treat close contacts.
care.why: Lice move by crawling and need close contact to spread, so checking contacts and avoiding shared personal items helps limit spread. The report’s own range and your doctor’s plan come first for any specific product choice.

about.reply: Head lice are tiny insects about the size of sesame seeds that live on the human scalp and feed on blood. They spread mainly by close head-to-head contact, especially in young children, and rarely through shared hats or hairbrushes. Cleanliness does not prevent them and they do not spread disease.
about.why: Lice crawl and need human blood to survive, so person-to-person contact is the common cause. Itching is from an allergic reaction to bites, and sores can become infected from scratching.

care.reply: For a headache at home, rest in a quiet dark room, drink water and try gentle neck and shoulder relaxation, and use a pain reliever only as per the label if you normally can. Many tension-type headaches improve with rest, regular meals, sleep and stress-relief steps.
care.next_step: If the headache is new, severe, or not easing with rest and simple measures, get medical care today; otherwise monitor and see a doctor within 2 to 3 days if it keeps coming back or interferes with daily life.
care.why: Tension headaches are common and often linked to stress, poor sleep, missed meals and muscle tightness, and lifestyle changes help. Headaches can also warn of a more serious problem, so red-flag signs need prompt care.
urgent_if: sudden severe headache
headache after a blow to the head
stiff neck with fever or confusion
loss of consciousness

about.reply: A headache is pain in the head or scalp and is the most common form of pain. The most common type is tension headache from tight muscles in the shoulders, neck, scalp and jaw, often linked to stress, poor sleep, missed meals, too much work or alcohol use. Other common types include migraine, cluster and sinus headaches.
about.why: Headaches are common and often improve with lifestyle changes, relaxation and pain relievers, but some can signal a more serious problem.

care.reply: Call 112 now. A heart attack is a medical emergency and needs emergency care right away, even if you are not sure it is a heart attack.
care.next_step: Call 112 now and keep the person still and calm while help is on the way. Do not give food or drink.
care.why: A heart attack happens when blood flow to the heart is suddenly blocked, so the heart muscle can start to die without quick treatment. Emergency services can start treatment as soon as they arrive.
urgent_if: Chest pain or pressure, or pain spreading to arm, jaw or back
Trouble breathing
Sweating, nausea, lightheadedness or sudden confusion
Person is unresponsive or not breathing normally

about.reply: A heart attack, also called myocardial infarction, is when blood flow to the heart is suddenly blocked so the heart muscle does not get oxygen and can begin to die if not treated quickly.
about.next_step: Call 112 right away if you or someone else has possible heart attack symptoms, even if you are not sure.
about.why: Blockage stops oxygen to heart muscle. Quick treatment can prevent or limit damage. Risk factors that can be changed include smoking, high cholesterol, high blood pressure and diabetes.

care.reply: Heart disease is a general term for many heart and blood vessel problems, including coronary artery disease, angina, heart attack, heart failure and rhythm problems. It cannot be managed from a name alone; a doctor needs to know the person’s symptoms, history and examination to know what is happening and what care is needed.
care.next_step: Book a medical check today for assessment, and get urgent care now if any warning signs appear.
care.why: Heart disease has many different types and causes, some present with chest discomfort, breathlessness or fatigue and some with no early symptoms. The evidence shows coronary artery disease is the most common type and can lead to angina, heart attack and heart failure, so evaluation is needed rather than self-management.
urgent_if: Chest pain or pressure, especially spreading to arm, jaw or back
Trouble breathing or sudden shortness of breath
Fainting, confusion or sudden weakness on one side
Heart racing, irregular or very slow pulse

about.reply: Heart disease is a general term for many problems with the heart and blood vessels, and the most common type is coronary artery disease where plaque builds up in the arteries that supply the heart muscle.
about.next_step: Talk to a doctor if you have chest pain or pressure, shortness of breath, palpitations, or a family history of early heart disease, so they can check your risk and plan.
about.why: Plaque buildup narrows or blocks blood flow to the heart and can lead to angina, heart attack, heart failure or abnormal rhythm. Causes vary by type and can include lifestyle, genetics, infections, medicines and other diseases.

care.reply: Heart failure means the heart can’t pump enough oxygen-rich blood to meet the body’s needs. It does not mean the heart has stopped, but without enough blood flow organs may not work well and problems can become serious. It can affect the left side, right side, or both, and it usually develops slowly from long-term conditions.
care.next_step: Have the person seen by a doctor soon for assessment and a care plan, and follow the doctor’s instructions for daily weight checks, medicines and activity limits.
care.why: Heart failure is a general term for a pump problem, not a single illness, and management depends on the cause and which side is involved. What is safe to do now depends on their current symptoms and doctor’s plan.
urgent_if: Trouble breathing or very shortness of breath, especially at rest or lying flat
Chest pain or pressure
Sudden confusion, fainting or not responding
Rapid weight gain with swelling in legs, ankles or abdomen

about.reply: Heart failure means your heart can't pump enough oxygen-rich blood to meet your body's needs, not that the heart has stopped beating. It can affect the left side, right side, or both, and often develops slowly from long-term conditions.
about.why: Heart failure is a pump problem, not a stoppage, and left-sided failure is more common than right-sided. It usually develops slowly from conditions that damage or stiffen the heart muscle.

care.reply: Heartburn is a burning feeling in the chest or throat from stomach acid backing up into the food pipe. For now avoid common triggers like spicy or fatty foods, alcohol, lying down soon after eating, and try smaller meals and sitting upright after eating.
care.why: Reflux can damage the esophagus over time, and heartburn can be worsened by pregnancy, certain foods, alcohol and some medicines. The report’s own advice and a doctor’s plan come first.
urgent_if: crushing chest pain or pressure
pain spreading to arm, jaw or back
trouble breathing
sudden worst headache

about.reply: Heartburn is a painful burning feeling in your chest or throat that happens when stomach acid backs up into the esophagus, the tube that carries food from your mouth to your stomach.
about.why: Acid reflux can damage the esophagus over time, and frequent heartburn may mean GERD. Pregnancy, certain foods, alcohol and some medicines can commonly bring it on.
urgent_if: crushing chest pain
chest pain spreading to arm, jaw or back
trouble breathing

care.reply: Move the person out of the heat to a cool, shaded or air-conditioned place now, loosen tight clothing and help them rest while you try to cool them with cool water or a fan. Offer small sips of water if they are awake and able to swallow safely, and do not give alcohol.
care.next_step: Get medical help right away today if there are signs of heat stroke, and seek care within 2 to 3 hours for heat exhaustion that is not improving with rest, cooling and fluids.
care.why: Heat illness happens when the body cannot cool itself enough, and heat exhaustion can progress to life-threatening heat stroke. Older adults, young children, sick people and those on certain medicines are at higher risk.
urgent_if: Body temperature very high, confusion or drowsiness
Dry skin with rapid strong pulse
Dizziness, nausea or fainting
Not responding or trouble breathing

about.reply: Heat illness happens when your body cannot cool itself enough in hot, humid weather and your body temperature rises to a dangerous level. It is commonly caused by staying out in the heat too long, exercising or working outside in high heat, dehydration, and risk is higher in older adults, young children, people who are sick or overweight, and with certain medicines or alcohol.
about.next_step: Get medical help right away if you or someone else has signs of heat stroke such as confusion, dizziness, nausea, dry skin, rapid strong pulse, or body temperature above 106°F (41°C).
about.why: Sweating normally cools the body, but in high heat and humidity sweating is not enough, so heat builds up and can progress from heat exhaustion to life-threatening heat stroke.
urgent_if: confusion or drowsiness
body temperature above 106°F (41°C)
dry skin with rapid strong pulse
dizziness, nausea with heat exposure

care.reply: Hemorrhoids are swollen veins around the anus or lower rectum from too much pressure, and symptoms differ by type. For now, general comfort measures are to avoid straining on the toilet, not sit for long periods, and keep the anal area clean and gentle; increasing fiber and fluids with food is commonly advised for bowel regularity.
care.next_step: If symptoms are mild, try gentle care at home for a few days and watch for change; see a doctor within 2 to 3 days if bleeding, pain, a lump, or prolapse is present, or if symptoms are not improving.
care.why: Pressure from straining, constipation, prolonged sitting and low fiber can worsen hemorrhoids, and external hemorrhoids often improve in days while internal ones can bleed or prolapse. The report’s own range and a clinician’s exam decide what is needed for this person.
urgent_if: heavy or ongoing rectal bleeding
sudden severe anal pain with fever
a prolapsed hemorrhoid that cannot be gently pushed back and is very painful

about.reply: Hemorrhoids are swollen, inflamed veins around the anus or lower rectum. They can be external under the skin near the anus or internal inside the anal canal and lower rectum.
about.why: They happen when too much pressure builds on anal veins, often from straining with bowel movements, chronic constipation or diarrhea, low-fiber diet, long toilet sitting, pregnancy, aging and heavy lifting. The report's own range and your doctor's plan come first for personal advice.

care.reply: Hepatitis means inflammation of the liver, and it can be caused by viruses, alcohol, medicines or poisons, or an immune attack. Because the cause and severity vary a lot, a person with suspected hepatitis needs a medical assessment to find the cause and check how the liver is working.
care.next_step: Arrange a doctor visit today for evaluation, and do not give alcohol, new medicines or supplements until reviewed.
care.why: Liver inflammation can be acute or chronic and may affect liver function. Only a clinician with tests can identify the type and decide care, and some causes need urgent treatment.
urgent_if: Yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine or pale stools
Confusion, extreme sleepiness or not waking up normally
Persistent vomiting, abdominal swelling or pain
Bleeding gums, nosebleeds or vomiting blood

about.reply: Hepatitis is inflammation and swelling of the liver that can damage how the liver works. It can be short-term acute or long-term chronic. The most common causes are viral hepatitis A, B, C, D and E, plus heavy alcohol use, certain medicines, chemicals or poisons, and autoimmune attack on the liver.
about.next_step: See a doctor promptly for yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, pale stools, ongoing nausea or loss of appetite, fever, fatigue that does not improve, or known exposure to hepatitis.
about.why: Inflammation from viruses, alcohol, toxins or immune attack can impair liver function. The type of cause and whether infection is acute or chronic changes care, so a clinician needs to assess symptoms and risk.

care.reply: Hepatitis A is a viral liver infection that is usually short-term and often improves with rest and fluids, but it spreads easily through contact with infected stool. At home, focus on strict handwashing after toilet use and before food handling, avoid preparing food for others, and keep the person’s waste separate until a doctor advises otherwise.
care.next_step: Have the person seen by a doctor today for assessment, guidance on isolation and prevention at home, and to check liver function.
care.why: The hepatitis A virus spreads by contact with an infected person’s stool, for example through unwashed hands, contaminated food or water, and close personal contact. A clinician can confirm the illness, advise on home care and how to protect others, and watch for complications.
urgent_if: confusion or drowsiness
persistent vomiting and cannot keep fluids down
severe abdominal pain
yellowing of eyes or skin getting worse

about.reply: Hepatitis A is a short-term viral infection that causes inflammation and swelling of the liver, and most people recover without treatment in a few weeks.
about.next_step: See a doctor promptly if you develop yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, pale stools, loss of appetite, nausea, fatigue or abdominal pain, especially after possible exposure.
about.why: It is caused by the hepatitis A virus which spreads through contact with an infected person's stool, for example via contaminated food or water, poor hand hygiene after using the bathroom, close personal contact, or sharing illegal drugs.

care.reply: Hepatitis B is a viral infection that causes inflammation of the liver and can be acute or chronic. It spreads through contact with blood, semen or other body fluids from an infected person, and household spread is reduced by not sharing razors, toothbrushes, nail clippers and by safe handling of blood.
care.next_step: Have the person see a doctor within the next few days for testing and advice on care and household precautions, and make sure close contacts know about vaccination.
care.why: A doctor can confirm the infection, check liver function and decide if treatment or monitoring is needed. Vaccination and avoiding sharing personal items lower the risk of spread to others at home.
urgent_if: yellowing of skin or eyes
confusion or extreme sleepiness
vomiting blood or black stools
severe abdominal pain

about.reply: Hepatitis B is a viral infection that causes inflammation and swelling of the liver, which can affect how well the liver works. It is caused by the hepatitis B virus that spreads through contact with blood, semen or other body fluids from an infected person.
about.next_step: See a doctor promptly if you have yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, pale stools, ongoing fatigue, loss of appetite, nausea, or abdominal pain, or if you were exposed to blood or body fluids and are unsure about vaccination or testing.
about.why: The virus can cause acute infection that often resolves on its own, or chronic infection that may need treatment. Risk is higher with exposure to infected blood or body fluids, unprotected sex, sharing razors or toothbrushes, and birth from an infected mother.

care.reply: High blood pressure usually has no symptoms, so it is found only by regular blood pressure checks.
care.next_step: If you have a recent reading, note the numbers and the time it was taken and book a check with a doctor within the next few days for repeat measurements. If the reading is higher than 180 systolic and higher than 120 diastolic, seek medical care right away.
care.why: Blood pressure varies during the day and with stress, so repeated checks are needed to know the usual level. Very high readings can be dangerous and need prompt attention.
urgent_if: Blood pressure higher than 180 and higher than 120
Chest pain or pressure
Trouble breathing
Sudden weakness, face droop or strange speech

about.reply: High blood pressure is the force of your blood pushing against artery walls. It is recorded as two numbers, systolic over diastolic, for example 120/80, and it usually has no symptoms so it is found only by regular checks.
about.why: Blood pressure rises when the heart pumps and falls between beats. Diagnosis needs two or more readings at separate visits because a single reading can vary.

care.reply: Hives are red, sometimes itchy raised bumps on the skin that often come from an allergic reaction to a drug or food, and can also be triggered by infections or stress. For mild hives with no breathing trouble, keep the skin cool, avoid scratching and known triggers, and watch how they change.
care.next_step: If hives last more than 2 to 3 days, spread quickly, come back often, or you are unsure of the cause, get a doctor’s review within 2 to 3 days.
care.why: Hives often fade on their own, but allergic reactions can sometimes lead to swelling in the airways which is a medical emergency. The report’s own range and your doctor’s plan come first for any medicine decisions.
urgent_if: trouble breathing or wheezing
swelling of lips, tongue or throat
hives with dizziness or feeling faint
rapidly spreading swelling

about.reply: Hives are red, raised, sometimes itchy bumps on the skin caused by your body releasing chemicals that make the skin swell. They are commonly triggered by an allergic reaction to a drug or food, and can also be linked to infections and stress.
about.next_step: See a doctor today if hives are widespread, painful, last more than a few days, or you need medicine to control them.
about.why: Allergic reactions are a common cause, and people with other allergies are more likely to get hives. Hives often go away on their own, but a serious case may need medicine.
urgent_if: trouble breathing
swelling of lips, tongue or throat
wheezing or noisy breathing
feeling faint or very unwell

care.reply: Hyperglycemia means high blood glucose, which most often affects people with diabetes when glucose stays in the blood instead of getting into cells for energy. At home, the safest step is to follow the person’s usual diabetes care plan and check their blood glucose as their doctor has advised, and not to change medicines on your own.
care.next_step: Contact their doctor today for guidance on this high reading and what to monitor, and seek care now if they have diabetes and are sick, stressed, or not eating normally.
care.why: Blood glucose rises with food, missed medicines, inactivity, stress or illness, and can stay high in diabetes when insulin is not enough or not working well. What is safe to do next depends on their known plan, recent readings and symptoms.
urgent_if: confused, drowsy or hard to wake
vomiting and unable to keep fluids down
rapid or deep breathing, fruity-smelling breath
chest pain or trouble breathing

about.reply: Hyperglycemia means high blood glucose, or high blood sugar in your blood. It most often affects people with diabetes because the body does not make enough insulin or cannot use it well, so glucose stays in the blood instead of reaching cells for energy.
about.why: Blood glucose rises after food and is normally lowered by insulin from the pancreas. When insulin action is low or medicines, food and activity are not balanced, glucose can build up, and stress or illness can also raise it.

care.reply: Hyperthyroidism means the thyroid gland is making more thyroid hormone than the body needs, which can affect heart rate, breathing, weight, digestion and mood. It is a medical condition that needs a doctor’s evaluation and ongoing care, not home treatment alone.
care.next_step: Book a doctor appointment within the next few days for assessment and guidance, and keep a note of symptoms and any medicines or supplements being used.
care.why: Thyroid hormones control many body functions, and untreated overactivity can affect heart, bones, muscles and menstrual cycle and fertility. The cause and best management depend on examination and tests, so a clinician’s plan comes first.
urgent_if: chest pain or pressure
very fast or irregular heartbeat
trouble breathing
sudden confusion or drowsiness

about.reply: Hyperthyroidism means your thyroid gland in the front of your neck makes too much thyroid hormone, which speeds up how your body uses energy and can affect heart rate, weight, digestion, mood and more.
about.why: The thyroid hormones control many body functions, so too much can strain the heart, bones and menstrual cycle if not treated. Common causes include Graves' disease, overactive thyroid nodules, thyroiditis with hormone leakage, and too much iodine from medicines or supplements.

care.reply: Call 112 now. Hypoglycemia means low blood glucose, and for many people with diabetes it is usually considered below 70 mg/dL, while for people without diabetes it is typically below 55 mg/dL. If the person is awake and can swallow safely, giving a sugary drink or sweets now is first aid for low blood sugar, and if they are confused, drowsy, not responding or not getting better, call 112 now.
care.next_step: Check if they are awake and can swallow safely; if yes give a sugary drink or sweets now and recheck how they feel in 15 minutes. If they are confused, drowsy, not responding, or cannot swallow safely, call 112 now.
care.why: Low glucose can cause shakiness, sweating, confusion and drowsiness because the brain needs glucose for energy. The exact low threshold can differ per person, so their health care team’s target matters.
urgent_if: Not responding or unconscious
Confused, drowsy or cannot stay awake
Trouble breathing
Seizure or fit

about.reply: Hypoglycemia means low blood glucose, or blood sugar, which is the main sugar in your blood that gives your body energy. For many people with diabetes it is usually considered low when blood glucose is below 70 mg/dL, and for people without diabetes it is typically below 55 mg/dL, though your personal target can be different.
about.next_step: If you have diabetes and get repeated low readings or symptoms like shakiness, sweating, hunger, confusion or drowsiness, talk to your doctor within 2 to 3 days to review your medicines, meals and monitoring plan.
about.why: Low glucose happens when blood sugar drops below what is healthy for you. In diabetes it is common with insulin or medicines that make the pancreas release more insulin, which can lower blood glucose too much.
urgent_if: confused or drowsy and cannot swallow safely
not responding or not breathing normally
seizure or fainting

care.reply: Hypothyroidism means the thyroid gland is not making enough thyroid hormone, so many body functions can slow down such as energy use, heart rate, digestion, mood and weight. It is a medical condition that needs a doctor’s evaluation and ongoing follow-up, not home treatment alone.
care.next_step: Book a doctor appointment within the next few days for assessment and to discuss testing and treatment options.
care.why: Thyroid hormones affect nearly every organ, and treatment is available but must be guided by a doctor who can confirm the cause and monitor safely. The evidence describes common causes like Hashimoto’s disease, thyroiditis, surgery, radiation and medicines.

about.reply: Hypothyroidism means your thyroid gland in the front of your neck makes too little thyroid hormone, so many body functions like heart rate, digestion, weight, mood and energy use slow down. The most common cause is Hashimoto's disease, an autoimmune condition where the immune system attacks the thyroid, and other causes include thyroid inflammation, thyroid surgery or radiation, certain medicines, and pituitary or iodine problems.
about.next_step: If you have ongoing tiredness, weight gain, feeling cold, dry skin, constipation, slowed heart rate, or low mood, book a check with your doctor within the next 1 to 2 weeks for thyroid tests.
about.why: Thyroid hormones control how the body uses energy and affect nearly every organ. Without enough hormone, functions slow down, but treatment is available and a doctor can confirm with blood tests.

care.reply: Indigestion is a burning or uncomfortable feeling in the upper abdomen, often with heartburn, belching, bloating or nausea, and it can be triggered by eating too much or too fast, fatty foods, stress, smoking, alcohol or some medicines.
care.next_step: Try avoiding foods and situations that seem to bring it on and see a health care provider if it lasts more than two weeks, or sooner if pain is severe or other symptoms appear.
care.why: Many common triggers can cause indigestion, but it can also be a sign of a digestive tract problem like an ulcer or GERD, so ongoing or severe symptoms need medical assessment.

about.reply: Indigestion is a discomfort or burning feeling in the upper abdomen, often with heartburn, belching, bloating, nausea or vomiting. It commonly follows eating too much or too fast, high-fat foods, stress, smoking, too much alcohol, tiredness, some medicines, and sometimes digestive problems like ulcer or GERD.
about.why: These are the typical symptoms and common triggers described for indigestion. The cause can be lifestyle-related or due to an underlying digestive problem, which is why duration and severity matter.

about.reply: Infant and newborn care means the daily care and health support a baby needs in the first weeks to months of life, like frequent feeding, diaper changes, sleep, warmth, hygiene and watching for normal changes as they grow.
about.why: Newborns have different needs and common skin issues like diaper rash and cradle cap, and parents often feel unsure at first. A health care provider can guide you on normal care and when to seek help.

care.reply: Insomnia means trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking unrefreshed, and it can be short-term from stress or longer-lasting when linked to other problems, medicines, caffeine, tobacco, alcohol or shift work.
care.next_step: Try regular sleep-wake times, a calm wind-down routine, limit caffeine, tobacco and alcohol, and avoid screens and long naps today; see a doctor if sleep problems last more than a month, happen most nights, or affect daytime functioning, mood or safety.
care.why: Acute insomnia often lasts days to weeks with stress, while chronic insomnia lasts a month or longer and is often secondary to another condition or habit. The report’s own range and a doctor’s plan come first for individual care.

about.reply: Insomnia is a common sleep disorder where you have trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or both, so you get too little or poor-quality sleep and do not feel refreshed on waking. It can be short-term acute lasting days to weeks, often from stress, work or family pressures, or a traumatic event, or chronic lasting a month or longer, often linked to medical conditions, medicines, caffeine, tobacco, alcohol, depression or emotional distress, shift work and travel.
about.next_step: Consider seeing a doctor if sleep problems last more than a month, happen at least 3 nights a week, or are affecting your daytime energy, mood or work, or if you are unsure what is causing it.
about.why: Acute insomnia is usually temporary and linked to stress, while chronic insomnia is often secondary to another problem or long-lasting stress and emotional upset. The cause is not always clear, so a doctor can help find triggers and check for other conditions.

about.reply: Iron is a mineral your body uses to make hemoglobin in red blood cells, which carries oxygen to all parts of the body and supports muscles, bone marrow and organ function.
about.why: Low iron can happen from blood loss, poor diet or trouble absorbing iron from food. People at higher risk include those with heavy periods, pregnancy or breastfeeding, infants, frequent blood donors and some chronic illnesses.

care.reply: Itching is an irritating sensation that makes you want to scratch, and it can be local or all over, sometimes with a rash or hives. For now you can try gentle care like cool compresses, regular moisturizing lotions, lukewarm or oatmeal baths, and avoid scratching, irritating fabrics and high heat and humidity.
care.next_step: Try these gentle measures today and note if itching is widespread, worsening, or has a rash; contact a health care provider if it is severe, does not improve after a few weeks, or has no clear cause.
care.why: Itching is a symptom of many conditions such as skin dryness, eczema, allergies, irritants and infections, and most cases improve with skin care. The cause is not known from description alone, so a clinician needs to see it if it persists.
urgent_if: trouble breathing
swelling of lips, tongue or throat
widespread hives with dizziness

about.reply: Itching is an irritating sensation that makes you want to scratch your skin. It can be in one area or all over and may come with a rash or hives. Common causes include dry skin, eczema, psoriasis, allergic reactions to food, insect bites, pollen or medicines, irritating chemicals or cosmetics, parasites like scabies, and sometimes liver, kidney, thyroid or nerve-related conditions.
about.why: Itching is a symptom, not a disease, so many different skin and internal conditions can cause it. The cause determines treatment, which is why persistent itching needs review.

care.reply: Joint disorders affect the bones and the soft tissues around them, such as cartilage, tendons and ligaments, and often cause joint pain with stiffness, redness or swelling. At home, keep the joint rested, avoid overuse, and use gentle movement as tolerated while watching for changes.
care.next_step: Book a doctor visit within 2 to 3 days if pain, stiffness, redness or swelling is present, or sooner if it is new, worsening or limits daily activities.
care.why: Many joint problems are chronic and can be worsened by repeated overuse or injury. A clinician can examine the joint, check for injury or disease and advise safe care.
urgent_if: cannot move the joint or it looks deformed
joint is very hot, red and swollen with fever
sudden severe pain after an injury
not able to bear weight or walk

about.reply: Joint disorders are problems that affect where two or more bones meet, including the bones themselves and the soft tissues around them like cartilage, tendons and ligaments.
about.why: Joints can be injured by overuse or sudden accidents, and diseases like arthritis can cause pain, stiffness, redness or swelling that often lasts a long time.

care.reply: Kidney failure means the kidneys are not cleaning blood and balancing fluid and minerals properly, so harmful wastes can build up and blood pressure and fluid balance can be affected. This is a serious medical condition that needs in-person care now, not home management alone.
care.next_step: Get medical care today for the person at home, and do not wait for symptoms to improve on their own.
care.why: When kidneys are damaged they stop removing excess fluid, minerals and wastes and making hormones needed for blood and bones, which can lead to dangerous buildup. The exact plan depends on how advanced it is and what the doctor finds.
urgent_if: trouble breathing or very fast breathing
sudden swelling of face, legs or abdomen with shortness of breath
confusion, drowsiness or not waking up normally
chest pain or pressure

about.reply: Kidney failure means the kidneys can no longer clean your blood, balance fluids and minerals, and make hormones properly, so wastes and fluid can build up in the body. It can develop from long-standing high blood pressure or diabetes, chronic infections, kidney stones, autoimmune disease, and some medicines, and it often progresses slowly over years.
about.next_step: Talk to a doctor promptly if you have swelling in the legs or face, much less or no urine, persistent fatigue, nausea, shortness of breath, or a sudden rise in blood pressure.
about.why: When kidneys are damaged they lose the ability to remove waste and excess fluid, which can raise blood pressure and affect red blood cells and bones. The exact cause and how far it has progressed can only be known with tests and a doctor's assessment.

care.reply: Kidney stones are solid pieces that can form in the kidney from urine substances and may pass on their own, but they can get stuck and cause severe pain. At home, keep the person hydrated with water if they can drink safely and rest comfortably while you watch for warning signs. Get medical care promptly for diagnosis with urine, blood and imaging tests, and for treatment if the stone does not pass.
care.next_step: Have the person seen by a doctor today for assessment, and seek urgent care now if any red-flag signs appear.
care.why: Pain can be extreme when a stone blocks urine flow, and signs like fever, blood in urine or vomiting mean infection or obstruction that needs prompt care. The doctor decides if the stone can pass on its own or needs shock waves, scope treatment or surgery.
urgent_if: Extreme back or side pain that will not go away
Fever and chills
Vomiting and cannot keep fluids down
Blood in urine with fever or cloudy bad-smelling urine

about.reply: A kidney stone is a solid piece of material that forms in the kidney from substances in the urine. It can be as small as a grain of sand or larger, and most pass on their own, but some get stuck and block urine flow causing great pain.
about.why: Kidney stones form when substances in urine concentrate and harden. The evidence describes signs that need medical help but does not list specific causes.

about.reply: Kidney tests are blood, urine and imaging checks that show how well your kidneys filter waste and make urine. Early kidney disease usually has no signs, so testing is the only way to know how your kidneys are doing.
about.why: Kidneys filter blood and remove waste. Tests like GFR, creatinine, albumin urine and ultrasound are used to check kidney function and structure. Risk factors that make checking important are diabetes, high blood pressure, heart disease and a family history of kidney failure.

care.reply: Knee problems can cause pain, swelling and difficulty walking, and they can come from worn cartilage like osteoarthritis or from injuries to ligaments, tendons and other structures. At home, rest the knee, avoid twisting or heavy loading, and keep it comfortable while you watch for changes.
care.next_step: Get a doctor seen within 2 to 3 days if pain is ongoing, walking is difficult, or there is swelling, locking or giving way; seek care sooner if it started after a twist or fall.
care.why: Treatment depends on the cause, which can range from wear-related changes to ligament or tendon injury, and a clinician needs to examine the knee to decide what is safe next. The evidence describes common causes but does not tell which one this person has.
urgent_if: cannot bear weight at all
knee is very swollen, hot and red with fever
knee locks and cannot move
sudden giving way after a twist or fall

about.reply: Knee injuries and disorders are problems with the knee joint's bones, cartilage, ligaments, tendons, muscles and fluid that cause pain and difficulty walking. The most common cause is osteoarthritis where knee cartilage gradually wears away, and injuries like ACL tear from sudden twisting are also common, especially in sports.
about.next_step: See a doctor within 2 to 3 days if knee pain is new, getting worse, makes walking or getting up from a chair hard, or is swollen and warm.
about.why: Knee problems are very common in all ages and can interfere with daily activities. Treatment depends on the cause, and a doctor can check the joint and advise care.

about.reply: LDL is low-density lipoprotein, often called 'bad' cholesterol. It carries cholesterol through your blood and when levels are high it can build up as plaque in arteries, which raises risk of coronary artery disease.
about.next_step: If you have risk factors like family history of heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, smoking or an unhealthy diet, ask your doctor when to check a lipid profile.
about.why: LDL carries cholesterol to body tissues. Too much LDL plus other substances forms plaque that narrows arteries over time. Causes are not certain for an individual, but diet high in saturated fat and trans fat, little physical activity, smoking, excess weight and genetics commonly raise LDL.

about.reply: Laboratory tests are checks of a sample of your blood, urine or body tissues to see if results fall within a normal range for you.
about.why: Results are compared to ranges because normal differs by person and can be affected by sex, age, diet, medicines and how you followed pre-test instructions. Doctors use them for routine checkups, diagnosis, treatment planning and monitoring.

care.reply: Liver disease is a group of conditions that can affect how the liver digests food, stores energy and removes poisons, and it can be caused by viruses, alcohol, medicines, poisons, fat buildup, inherited conditions and cancer. It often has no symptoms early on, but can cause swelling of the abdomen and legs, easy bruising, changes in stool and urine colour, and yellowing of the skin and eyes. A doctor needs to check with history, exam and tests such as liver function tests and imaging to find the cause and guide care.
care.next_step: Book a doctor appointment within the next few days for assessment, and do not start or stop medicines or alcohol on your own.
care.why: Symptoms vary and sometimes are absent, so only a clinician who can examine the person and order tests can tell what is happening and what care is needed. The evidence describes common signs but does not predict this person’s situation.
urgent_if: yellowing of skin or eyes
swelling of abdomen or legs with confusion
vomiting blood or black stools
severe abdominal pain

about.reply: Liver disease means the liver is damaged and cannot do its jobs of digesting food, storing energy and removing poisons. Common causes are viruses like hepatitis A, B and C, alcohol use, medicines or poisons, fatty liver disease, cirrhosis, liver cancer and inherited conditions. See a doctor if you have swelling of the abdomen or legs, easy bruising, yellowing of skin or eyes, changes in stool or urine colour, or no symptoms but risk factors for liver disease.
about.next_step: Book a check with your doctor within 2 to 3 days if you have any of those symptoms or known risk factors like heavy alcohol use or viral hepatitis exposure.
about.why: The liver can be injured by infections, alcohol, drugs and metabolic conditions, and damage may be silent at first. Tests like liver function tests and imaging can check for damage and guide care.

care.reply: For now keep the person safe by having them sit or lie down, rise slowly from lying to standing, and drink water if they are able to swallow safely.
care.next_step: If there are no symptoms of dizziness, fainting or confusion, you can note the reading and check again later in the day; if symptoms are present, get medical care today.
care.why: Some people have naturally low readings with no symptoms, while a drop can be due to a medical condition or medicines. The report's own range and a doctor's plan come first.
urgent_if: fainting or not waking up
confusion or drowsiness
chest pain or pressure
trouble breathing

about.reply: Low blood pressure means the force of your blood pushing against artery walls is lower than usual, often a reading of 90/60 mmHg or lower. It can be normal for some people all the time with no symptoms, or it can drop because of a medical condition, certain medicines, or standing up too quickly.
about.next_step: See a doctor within 2 to 3 days if you have dizziness, fainting, or symptoms when standing, or if low readings are new for you.
about.why: Blood pressure is systolic over diastolic, e.g., 120/80. Low blood pressure is a problem mainly when it causes dizziness, fainting or shock, not just the number alone.

care.reply: Malaria is a serious infection that needs prompt in-person medical care, not home treatment. Get the person checked today for a blood test and treatment, and do not wait to see if it improves.
care.next_step: Take the person to a doctor or clinic today for evaluation; if fever, chills or flu-like symptoms are present now, seek care urgently.
care.why: Malaria can be life-threatening and requires a blood test to confirm and specific medicines chosen by a doctor based on the type and where the infection was acquired.
urgent_if: fever with chills or shaking
vomiting and cannot keep fluids down
jaundice, confusion or drowsiness
trouble breathing or very weak

about.reply: Malaria is a serious infection caused by a parasite that is spread to people by the bite of an infected mosquito. It is most common in warm countries and can cause fever, chills, flu-like symptoms, vomiting, diarrhea and jaundice. See a doctor promptly if you have fever and chills, especially after travel to an area where malaria occurs.
about.next_step: If you have fever after travel to a malaria area, seek medical care the same day for testing.
about.why: The parasite is transmitted by mosquito bites and can become life-threatening, but it can be diagnosed with a blood test and treated with drugs chosen based on the type and location of infection.

care.reply: Medication errors can happen at home and are best prevented by knowing your medicines, reading labels each time, and keeping an up-to-date list of all medicines, doses and allergies to take to every visit. If you are unsure whether the right medicine was given or how it should be taken, check the label now and ask the pharmacist or doctor before taking it.
care.next_step: Check the medicine name, label directions and your personal medicine list today, and call your pharmacist or doctor today for clarification if anything is unclear.
care.why: Errors often come from confusion about name, dose timing or duration, and from not knowing allergies or interactions. A clear list and label check reduces mistakes, but only the prescriber or pharmacist can confirm what is correct for this person.
urgent_if: trouble breathing
swelling of face lips tongue or throat
chest pain or pressure
severe drowsiness or confusion

about.reply: Medication errors are mistakes that happen when medicines are not used correctly, which can cause harmful reactions instead of helping. They can occur in hospital, clinic, pharmacy or at home, often from not knowing the medicine name, dose timing or duration, mixing medicines, or relying on memory instead of labels.
about.why: Medicines treat infections, prevent chronic problems and ease pain, but errors happen when the right medicine, dose, timing or duration is not followed. Keeping a written list and reading labels each time helps prevent many of these mistakes.

about.reply: Medicines are substances you take to treat illness, relieve symptoms, or prevent disease, such as tablets, syrups, injections or creams. They are made to help the body heal or feel better, but they can also cause side effects or interact with food, alcohol or other medicines.
about.why: Medicines are not a condition that is caused; they are treatments. Risks depend on the specific medicine, dose and your health, so general safety advice applies.

about.reply: Menopause is the point when periods stop for 12 months in a row and pregnancy is no longer possible. It usually happens between ages 45 and 55, after a transition period called perimenopause that can last several years and often starts in your 40s.
about.next_step: Talk to a doctor if periods stop before age 45, if you have hot flushes, sleep or mood changes that bother you, or if you have questions about bone and heart health after menopause.
about.why: Menopause is a natural end of ovarian hormone production. Early or premature menopause before 40 or 45 can happen on its own, after surgery to remove ovaries, or after treatments like chemotherapy or hormone therapy for breast cancer.

about.reply: Menstruation, also called a period, is normal monthly vaginal bleeding that happens when the uterus sheds its lining because pregnancy did not occur. It is part of the menstrual cycle, usually about 28 days from the first day of one period to the first day of the next, and most periods last 3 to 7 days.
about.next_step: Talk to a doctor if bleeding is very heavy, lasts longer than 7 days, is very painful, or is irregular for more than a few years after periods started.
about.why: The cycle is driven by monthly hormonal changes that prepare the uterus for pregnancy. Periods can be shorter or longer and may take a few years to become regular, and changes can happen with childbirth, breastfeeding or approaching menopause.

about.reply: Mental disorders are conditions that affect thinking, feeling, mood and behavior, and can be short-term, come and go, or be long-lasting. They are not caused by character flaws or laziness.
about.why: Mental disorders can affect how you relate to others and function each day. Causes are not single; risk can involve genes, life experiences, biological factors, brain injury, prenatal exposures, substance use, medical illness and social isolation.

care.reply: For a migraine episode at home, rest in a dark quiet room, avoid bright light and loud sounds, and keep hydrated with small sips of water. These are general comfort measures and not a diagnosis.
care.next_step: If pain is not easing with rest and usual comfort measures, or if this is a new or different headache pattern, get medical advice within 2 to 3 days.
care.why: Migraines are recurring headaches often with throbbing pain, nausea and sensitivity to light and sound, and triggers vary by person. What helps now is general comfort and avoiding known triggers, but a doctor is needed to confirm the pattern and plan care.
urgent_if: Sudden worst headache ever
New confusion, weakness or trouble speaking
Fever with neck stiffness
Headache after a head injury

about.reply: Migraine is a recurring headache that usually causes moderate to severe throbbing pain, often on one side of the head, and can come with nausea, sensitivity to light and sound, and weakness.
about.why: It is thought to have a genetic basis and is triggered by personal factors such as stress, sleep changes, hormonal changes, bright lights, loud noises, strong smells, skipped meals, caffeine changes, and certain foods. Triggers vary from person to person so the exact cause for an individual is not certain.

care.reply: Muscle cramps are sudden involuntary muscle spasms that are common and often happen after exercise or at night, especially in the legs, thighs, feet, hands, arms, abdomen or ribcage area. Right now you can gently stretch the cramped muscle, massage it, apply a warm compress and make sure the person drinks water.
care.next_step: Try gentle stretching, massage and warmth now, and keep hydrated; if cramps are severe, happen often, or do not ease with stretching and fluids, contact a health care provider within 2 to 3 days.
care.why: Cramps are often from straining a muscle, dehydration or low electrolytes, and usually ease in minutes. The cause is sometimes unknown and can be linked to nerve compression, pregnancy, certain medicines or medical conditions.

about.reply: Muscle cramps are sudden, involuntary painful contractions or spasms in a muscle that usually last seconds to minutes, most often in thighs, feet, calves, hands, arms, abdomen or ribcage area. They are very common and often happen after exercise or at night.
about.why: The cause is sometimes unknown.

care.reply: For nausea and vomiting at home, keep fluids down in small sips and rest, and avoid solid food until vomiting settles. This is general information only and not a diagnosis.
care.next_step: Watch for warning signs and contact a health care provider today if vomiting lasts more than 24 hours, or sooner if any urgent signs appear.
care.why: The cause determines treatment, so a provider needs history and exam to decide.
urgent_if: Vomiting for longer than 24 hours
Blood in the vomit
Severe abdominal pain
Severe headache and stiff neck

about.reply: Nausea is feeling sick to your stomach as if you are going to throw up, and vomiting is throwing up. It is common and can be caused by many things such as infections like gastroenteritis or food poisoning, motion sickness, migraines, pregnancy-related morning sickness, medicines, reflux or ulcers, and intestinal blockage.
about.why: Nausea and vomiting are symptoms, not a single illness, so the cause and needed care depend on what is triggering them and how long they last.

care.reply: Neck pain is very common and often comes from muscle strain or tension from overuse, awkward sleeping, exercise or a fall, and it can feel like it comes from the shoulder, jaw, head or upper arms.
care.next_step: At home, rest the neck, avoid awkward positions and prolonged computer work, apply ice as tolerated and use pain relievers only as directed on the label. If pain is not clearly improving in 2 to 3 days, or is severe, see a doctor within 2 to 3 days.
care.why: Most neck muscle strains improve with simple care, but treatment depends on the cause. Whiplash and other injuries can need physical therapy or a cervical collar, and surgery is rarely needed.
urgent_if: trouble breathing or swallowing
numbness or weakness in arms or hands
loss of bladder or bowel control
fever with neck pain or stiff neck

about.reply: Neck injuries and disorders are problems in any part of the neck — muscles, bones, joints, tendons, ligaments or nerves — that cause neck pain, which can also feel like pain in the shoulder, jaw, head or upper arms.
about.next_step: See a doctor within 2 to 3 days if pain is new, worsening, limits movement, or follows a fall or accident; seek care sooner if you have numbness, weakness, trouble walking, or pain after a car crash.
about.why: Muscle strain or tension from overuse, awkward sleeping, exercise, falls or accidents like whiplash are common causes. Treatment depends on cause and may include ice, pain relievers, physical therapy or a cervical collar, and surgery is rarely needed.

care.reply: Nose injuries and disorders cover many different problems, from a stuffy or runny nose to a broken nose, nosebleeds, nasal polyps, deviated septum and rhinitis. What to do now depends on the specific sign you are seeing, because care is different for a blocked nose, bleeding, pain after an injury or loss of smell.
care.next_step: If there is any nose injury, ongoing nosebleed, trouble breathing through the nose, severe pain, fever with nasal symptoms, or change in smell, get medical advice today; for a minor cold-like stuffy or runny nose, gentle supportive care at home is usually enough and see a doctor
care.why: The nose filters, warms and moistens air and supports smell, so problems can affect breathing, sleep and comfort. The evidence lists several common nose issues, but without a specific symptom it is not possible to say which applies or what treatment is needed.
urgent_if: heavy nosebleed not stopping after 15 minutes of firm pressure
trouble breathing or noisy breathing through the nose
severe facial pain or swelling after a hit
vomiting blood or blood in the mouth after a nose injury

about.reply: Nose injuries and disorders are problems that affect the nose’s job of filtering, warming and moistening air you breathe and helping your sense of smell. Common issues include a deviated septum, nasal polyps, nosebleeds, rhinitis from allergies, and nasal fractures or a broken nose.
about.next_step: See a doctor promptly for a nosebleed that won’t stop after 10 minutes of firm pressure, a visibly crooked or painful nose after an injury, trouble breathing through the nose, or symptoms that keep you from sleeping or daily activities.
about.why: When the nose is blocked or injured, breathing, sleep and comfort can suffer, and some problems like a fracture or persistent bleeding need in-person care. The exact cause and need for treatment depend on your history and exam.

about.reply: Nutrition is the way your body gets energy and nutrients from the foods and drinks you eat every day. It includes proteins, carbohydrates, fats, vitamins, minerals and water that help you grow, repair tissues and stay healthy. Good nutrition does not mean a strict diet, it means choosing a balanced variety of foods that fit your preferences, culture and budget.
about.why: Nutrients support weight, heart health, mood and lower risk of problems like type 2 diabetes and heart disease. The evidence describes nutrition as a general health support, not a condition with causes.

about.reply: Obesity is a disease where the body has too much body fat, not just weighing too much. It is usually identified by BMI, with an adult BMI of 30 or more considered obesity and 40 or higher severe obesity. It develops over time when calories taken in from food and drinks are more than calories used by activity and daily living, and risk is affected by genetics, eating habits, physical activity level, some medicines and medical conditions.
about.next_step: If you are concerned about your weight, BMI or health risks, book a check with your doctor within the next 1 to 2 weeks for assessment and advice.
about.why: Extra body fat, especially around the waist, raises risk for other diseases and health problems. The exact balance of calories and activity that is right for you is individual and not certain without a personal check.

about.reply: Older Adult Health is about how bodies and minds change with age and how to stay active and healthy as you get older. It covers normal aging changes and warning signs that may need medical care.
about.next_step: If you notice changes that worry you, talk to your health care provider soon.
about.why: Aging brings expected changes, but some changes can be signs of a medical problem. A healthy lifestyle with good eating, regular activity and mental health support helps manage normal aging.

about.reply: Older adult mental health is about emotional, psychological and social well-being in later life, and how it affects thinking, feeling, coping with stress and relating to others. It is not a normal part of aging, though many older adults feel satisfied with life even with illness.
about.next_step: Talk to a doctor within 2 to 3 days if you notice changes in mood or energy, eating or sleeping habits, or withdrawing from people and activities you enjoy.
about.why: Important life changes like loss of a loved one, retirement or serious illness can cause unease, stress and sadness. Some people have more trouble adjusting and can develop depression or anxiety, which can make chronic health problems harder to manage.

care.reply: Osteoarthritis is wear-and-tear arthritis that affects joints, most often hands, knees, hips, neck and lower back. It happens when joint cartilage breaks down so bones can rub, which can cause pain with movement that eases with rest, morning stiffness for up to 30 minutes, swelling after use, less movement and a loose feeling.
care.next_step: For general symptom care, keep the joint moving gently, use rest and heat or cold as tolerated, and avoid overloading it; book a routine check with a doctor within 2 to 3 days for a personal plan.
care.why: There is no cure and it usually worsens slowly, but symptoms can be managed. A doctor can confirm the joint problem, rule out other causes and suggest safe exercises, supports and pain management for this person.

about.reply: Osteoarthritis is the most common type of arthritis where the smooth cartilage that cushions the ends of bones in joints like hands, knees, hips, neck and lower back wears down and becomes rough, so bones can rub and bone spurs may form.
about.why: It usually develops slowly and has no cure, but symptoms can be managed. Researchers think it is caused by a mix of body and environment factors, and risk rises with age.

care.reply: Osteoporosis is a silent bone-weakening condition where more bone is broken down than replaced, so it often has no symptoms until a fracture happens, most commonly in the hip, spine or wrist.
care.next_step: Book a check-up with their doctor soon for bone health assessment and advice on safe movement and fall prevention.
care.why: Because osteoporosis usually causes no warning signs and risk rises with age, sex, body size and race, a doctor can check risk factors and decide if a bone density test is needed.
urgent_if: sudden severe bone or back pain
inability to bear weight or walk
visible deformity after a fall
new height loss or stooped posture

about.reply: Osteoporosis is a 'silent' disease where bones become weak and more likely to break because more bone is broken down than replaced. It often has no symptoms until a fracture happens, most commonly in the hip, spine vertebrae, or wrist.
about.next_step: If you are over 50, are a woman after menopause, are slim and thin-boned, or have a family history of fractures, ask your doctor about bone health screening within the next few weeks.
about.why: Bones are living tissue that is constantly renewed. With age and certain risk factors, bone loss outpaces rebuilding, which weakens structure and strength.

about.reply: Over-the-counter medicines are drugs you can buy without a prescription to relieve aches, pains, itches, or manage recurring problems like allergies and migraines. They are approved as safe and effective for general use when you follow the label instructions. They do not have a cause, they are medicines used for symptoms or prevention.
about.why: OTC medicines are regulated for self-care use, but risks remain from interactions, medical conditions, allergies and pregnancy. The label instructions should be followed and a pharmacist or health care provider can clarify use.

about.reply: Pain relievers are medicines that reduce or relieve headaches, sore muscles, arthritis and other aches and pains. Pain commonly happens with injury, inflammation or swelling, infection, muscle strain and conditions like arthritis or menstrual cramps. See a doctor if pain is severe, sudden, lasts more than a few days, is not helped by usual care, or comes with fever, chest pain, trouble breathing, vomiting blood, or signs of injury.
about.why: Pain relievers work in different ways, and OTC options like acetaminophen and NSAIDs are often used for mild to moderate pain, but each person responds differently and risks differ. The report notes acetaminophen is often considered safer but can be taken too much accidentally, and NSAIDs can cause stomach upset or ulcers if overused.

care.reply: Panic disorder is an anxiety condition with repeated panic attacks — sudden intense fear or discomfort with physical symptoms like rapid heartbeat — and often worry about more attacks and avoidance of places where attacks happened. Support now means a calm, safe space, slow breathing and reassurance, and avoid giving alcohol or sedatives.
care.next_step: Book a doctor appointment within the next few days for assessment and a care plan, and seek care sooner if attacks are frequent, worsening, or causing avoidance of daily life.
care.why: The cause is not fully known and may involve genetics and brain factors. Many people have one or two panic attacks without developing panic disorder, so a clinician needs to assess the pattern and rule out other causes.
urgent_if: Chest pain or pressure, trouble breathing, or symptoms that feel like a heart attack
Confusion, fainting, or not responding normally
Thoughts of harming self or hopelessness about living

about.reply: Panic disorder is an anxiety condition with repeated panic attacks — sudden intense fear or discomfort with physical symptoms like a pounding heartbeat, even when there is no real danger.
about.why: The exact cause is unknown, but genetics and brain factors may play a role.

care.reply: Parkinson's disease is a movement disorder linked to lower dopamine in the brain. It usually starts gradually, often on one side, with tremor, stiffness, slowness of movement and balance problems, and there is no single test for it; doctors diagnose it from history and neurological exam.
care.next_step: Book an appointment with a doctor soon for assessment and support, and keep a simple note of when symptoms started and how they change day to day.
care.why: Medicines and therapies can help symptoms dramatically and surgery or deep brain stimulation may help severe cases, but only a doctor who examines the person can confirm the diagnosis and plan care. The course varies a lot between people.

about.reply: Parkinson's disease is a movement disorder where nerve cells in the brain make less dopamine, leading to trembling, stiffness, slowness of movement and balance problems that often start on one side of the body.
about.next_step: See a doctor promptly if you notice gradual one-sided tremor, stiffness, slowness or balance trouble, or problems with walking, talking, chewing or swallowing.
about.why: It is not caused by one common thing; most cases are not clearly inherited and environmental chemical exposure may play a role in some people. There is no specific test, so diagnosis is by history and neurological exam.

care.reply: A peptic ulcer is a sore in the stomach or duodenum lining that often causes burning stomach pain that can come between meals or at night and may briefly ease with food or antacids. Do not start or stop medicines on your own; get a doctor to confirm the cause and plan treatment, as ulcers can worsen without care.
care.next_step: Book a doctor visit within 2 to 3 days for testing and advice, and seek care sooner if pain is severe or new warning signs appear.
care.why: The most common causes are Helicobacter pylori infection and long-term NSAID use, and diagnosis needs blood, breath or stool tests or endoscopy. Antacids and milk do not heal ulcers, and treatment may need acid-reducing medicines or antibiotics.
urgent_if: vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds
black tarry stools or visible blood in stool
severe sudden abdominal pain
fainting, dizziness or trouble breathing

about.reply: A peptic ulcer is a sore in the lining of your stomach or the first part of your small intestine, the duodenum, and the most common symptom is a burning stomach pain that can come and go for days or weeks. It is most commonly caused by infection with the bacterium Helicobacter pylori and by long-term use of NSAIDs such as aspirin and ibuprofen; stress and spicy foods do not cause ulcers but can make them worse.
about.next_step: If you have burning stomach pain that starts between meals or at night, or pain that eases briefly with food or antacids, book a doctor visit within 2 to 3 days for testing and advice.
about.why: Stomach acid damages the protective lining to form the sore, and ulcers will get worse if not treated. Diagnosis needs tests for H. pylori and sometimes an endoscopy or x-ray, which only a doctor can order.

care.reply: Pneumonia is an infection in one or both lungs that can range from mild to severe, and it needs a medical assessment to confirm the cause and decide treatment.
care.next_step: Get a doctor to see the person today for examination and tests; seek care now if breathing is hard or symptoms are worsening.
care.why: Pneumonia can be caused by bacteria, viruses or fungi and sometimes leads to bacterial infection after a viral illness. The severity depends on the germ and the person's overall health, so a clinician needs to evaluate them.
urgent_if: trouble breathing or fast breathing
chest pain or pressure
confusion or drowsiness
fever not coming down or worsening cough

about.reply: Pneumonia is an infection in one or both lungs that makes the tiny air sacs fill with fluid or pus, so breathing becomes harder. It is most commonly caused by bacteria such as Streptococcus pneumoniae, and can also be caused by viruses like flu, RSV and SARS-CoV-2, and less often by fungi in people with weakened immunity. See a doctor promptly for fever with cough, chest pain, fast or difficult breathing, or if symptoms are not improving.
about.next_step: If you have fever, cough with phlegm, chest pain or trouble breathing, get medical care today.
about.why: The infection type, age and overall health affect how severe pneumonia can be, and viral pneumonia can lead to bacterial pneumonia. The report's own range and a doctor's exam decide care.
urgent_if: trouble breathing or fast breathing
chest pain or pressure
confusion or drowsiness
fever not coming down

care.reply: Polycystic ovary syndrome is a hormonal disorder that can affect periods, ovulation and androgen levels, and it often runs in families. It is managed with a doctor’s plan for symptoms, menstrual regularity and long-term health, not with home treatment alone.
care.next_step: Book an appointment with a doctor soon for evaluation and a personalised management plan, and keep a note of periods, hair growth and any other symptoms to share.
care.why: The exact cause is not known and features vary between people, so a clinician needs to confirm the pattern and rule out other causes before advising care.

about.reply: Polycystic ovary syndrome, PCOS, is a common hormonal disorder that affects the ovaries and can cause irregular or absent periods, higher androgen levels leading to extra body or facial hair, and sometimes ovarian cysts. The exact cause is not known, but it tends to run in families and involves hormone and metabolic imbalances.
about.next_step: Talk to a doctor if you have irregular or missed periods, difficulty conceiving, sudden excess hair growth or acne, or signs of high blood sugar, so they can check you properly.
about.why: PCOS is defined by at least two of irregular ovulation, high androgens and ovarian follicle growths, and genetics and hormone imbalances are commonly involved. The evidence describes the features and that the exact cause is unknown.

about.reply: Prediabetes means your blood sugar is higher than normal but not high enough for diabetes, and it raises the risk for type 2 diabetes, heart disease and stroke over time.
about.why: It usually happens when the body has insulin resistance or does not make enough insulin, so glucose stays in the blood. Being overweight and not getting regular physical activity are major factors.

about.reply: Pregnancy is when a fertilized egg implants in the uterus and develops into a baby over about 9 months. It commonly happens when sperm from sexual intercourse fertilizes an egg released from the ovary. Regular prenatal visits with a health care provider are important to monitor your health and the baby's development, and you should see a provider promptly for any concerns such as bleeding, severe pain, fever, decreased fetal movement, or if you are unsure about medicines, nutrition or activity.
about.why: Fertilization during sex is the usual cause of pregnancy, and prenatal care helps find and treat problems early. The exact timing to seek care depends on symptoms and your provider's plan.

about.reply: Pregnancy and medicines is about whether medicines are safe when you are pregnant. Some medicines are safe, but many prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, herbs and supplements can harm the developing fetus, so you should check with your health care provider before taking any medicine.
about.next_step: Talk to your provider before you start, stop or change any medicine, and ask about prenatal vitamins at your prenatal care visits.
about.why: The risks and benefits of a medicine in pregnancy depend on the specific drug and your health condition. Not using needed medicine can also be harmful, so decisions are made together with your provider.

care.reply: Call 112 now. Rabies can be fatal once symptoms start and needs immediate medical care.
care.next_step: Go to the nearest hospital now for urgent evaluation; do not wait.
care.why: Rabies is a deadly virus spread by animal bites. Post-exposure shots can prevent it if given right away, but once symptoms appear the disease is usually fatal.
urgent_if: confusion, hallucinations or paralysis
fever with headache and fatigue after an animal bite
difficulty swallowing or breathing
not responding normally

about.reply: Rabies is a deadly virus infection spread mainly by the bite of an infected animal. It is commonly caused by bites from infected dogs, cats, farm animals, and wild animals like raccoons, skunks, bats and foxes.
about.next_step: If you have been bitten or scratched by an animal, wash the wound well and get medical care the same day for post-exposure shots.
about.why: The virus enters through broken skin from saliva. Once symptoms like fever, headache, confusion, hallucinations and paralysis start, the disease is usually fatal, but a series of shots can prevent it if given right away after exposure.

care.reply: A rash is an area of irritated or swollen skin that can be itchy, red, painful or have bumps and blisters, and it can be caused by many different things including irritants and allergies.
care.next_step: Keep the skin gentle and avoid scratching or known irritants, and have a health care provider look at it if it is bad, does not go away, or is getting worse within 2 to 3 days.
care.why: Rashes have many possible causes and the right care depends on what kind it is. Most mild rashes clear fairly quickly, but some need long-term treatment.
urgent_if: fever with spreading redness
blisters with raw skin and pain
swelling of lips tongue or throat or trouble breathing

about.reply: A rash is an area of irritated or swollen skin that can be itchy, red, painful, or have blisters and raw patches. It is a symptom, not a disease by itself, and commonly happens after contact with an irritant or allergen like chemicals or poison ivy, and from many other medical problems.
about.why: Rashes have many different causes, so the right care depends on what kind it is. Most clear up fairly quickly, but some are long-lasting and need treatment.

care.reply: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune condition that causes pain, swelling and stiffness in joints, often in the wrists and fingers, and can also affect eyes, skin, heart, nerves, blood or lungs. There is no cure, but early treatment can help manage symptoms and reduce joint damage. A doctor can confirm the diagnosis and make a care plan for the person at home.
care.next_step: Book a doctor visit within the next 2 to 3 days for assessment and ongoing management.
care.why: RA affects the joint lining and can cause progressive damage over time, so early medical care matters. The exact plan depends on the person’s history, exam and tests, which only a clinician can do.
urgent_if: fever with joint swelling
chest pain or trouble breathing
sudden severe joint pain or inability to move a joint
signs of infection

about.reply: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune condition where the immune system attacks the lining of joints, causing pain, swelling and stiffness, most often in the wrists and fingers. It can also cause inflammation in eyes, skin, heart, nerves, blood or lungs, and over time can make joints work less well. There is no cure, but early treatment can help manage symptoms and reduce joint damage.
about.next_step: See a doctor promptly if you have persistent joint pain, swelling or morning stiffness lasting more than a few weeks, or if joints become warm, red and hard to use.
about.why: RA is an autoimmune disease, not the same as age-related osteoarthritis, and risk is higher in women, smokers, people with a family history and some other medical conditions. Early care matters because inflammation can cause lasting joint damage.

care.reply: Salmonella infection usually causes fever, diarrhea, abdominal cramps and sometimes nausea or vomiting that often lasts 4 to 7 days, and most people recover with rest and fluids at home. Keep the person hydrated with clean water and oral rehydration solution, avoid anti-diarrheal medicines, and practice careful handwashing and toilet hygiene to avoid spreading it.
care.next_step: Get medical care today if diarrhea is frequent, there are signs of dehydration, fever is high or lasting, or the person is an infant, older adult or has chronic health problems. A doctor can confirm with a stool test and advise care.
