care.why: Symptoms are usually self-limited, but dehydration and bloodstream spread can be serious in vulnerable people. The report’s own range and the doctor’s plan come first.
urgent_if: Not able to drink or keep fluids down
Signs of dehydration: very little urine, dry mouth, dizziness on standing
Blood in stool
Fever higher than 39°C or lasting more than 3 days

about.reply: Salmonella is a group of bacteria that commonly causes foodborne illness. It is often found in raw poultry, eggs, beef, unwashed fruit and vegetables, and after handling pets like reptiles, and it usually causes fever, diarrhea, abdominal cramps and headache that last 4-7 days.
about.next_step: See a doctor promptly if diarrhea lasts more than a few days, you have high fever, signs of dehydration, or you are an infant, older adult or have chronic health problems.
about.why: Most people recover without treatment, but infection can be more serious in vulnerable groups and can spread to the bloodstream. A stool test is used for diagnosis and antibiotics are used when needed.

care.reply: Scabies is an itchy skin condition caused by a microscopic mite that spreads by close skin-to-skin contact and can spread in households and to sexual partners. A health care provider usually diagnoses it by looking at the rash and skin burrows, and treatment is with prescription lotions plus washing clothes, bedding and towels in hot water and drying on hot heat. Household members and sexual partners are usually treated at the same time.
care.next_step: Have the person seen a doctor today to confirm scabies and get the correct prescription treatment, and wash all clothes, bedding and towels in hot water and dry on hot heat today.
care.why: Diagnosis needs an in-person skin check and treatment is prescription lotion, not over-the-counter care. Washing linens helps reduce re-infestation because mites can survive briefly on fabrics, especially with crusted scabies.

about.reply: Scabies is an itchy skin condition caused by a microscopic mite called Sarcoptes scabiei that burrows in the skin. It spreads most commonly through close skin-to-skin contact with an infected person, and can also spread in crowded places and via sharing clothes, towels or bedding, especially with crusted scabies. You cannot get it from pets.
about.next_step: If you have intense itching especially at night, pimple-like rash or sores from scratching, see a doctor within 2 to 3 days for skin examination.
about.why: The mite causes intense itching and a rash, and diagnosis is by looking at the skin for burrows. Treatment needs prescription lotions and often household contacts need treatment too.

care.reply: Call 112 now. Keep the person safe now by moving hard objects away, placing them on their side if they are unconscious, and do not put anything in their mouth. Time the seizure and note what you see, because most seizures last 30 seconds to 2 minutes and stop on their own.
care.next_step: Call 112 now if the seizure lasts longer than 5 minutes, if another seizure starts before they wake up, or if they are injured, have trouble breathing, or are pregnant. Otherwise get medical care today for a first seizure or if they have not been evaluated before.
care.why: Seizures are symptoms of sudden abnormal brain electrical activity and can be caused by many things including medicines, high fever, head injury and brain disorders. What to do next depends on how long it lasts and whether they recover normally.
urgent_if: Seizure lasts longer than 5 minutes
Repeated seizures without waking up between them
Trouble breathing or injury during seizure
Person does not wake up normally after

about.reply: A seizure is a symptom of sudden abnormal electrical activity in the brain that can cause shaking or other changes in awareness, and not all seizures involve convulsions.
about.next_step: If you or someone you know has a seizure, seek medical care promptly for evaluation.
about.why: Seizures can be caused by many things including medicines, high fevers, head injuries and certain brain disorders, and most last 30 seconds to 2 minutes. Recurring seizures due to a brain disorder can be epilepsy, but only a doctor can determine the cause for a person.

care.reply: Call 112 now. Sepsis is a life-threatening medical emergency and needs immediate in-person care, not home treatment.
care.next_step: Call 112 now and get the person to the nearest emergency department immediately. Do not wait to see if it improves.
care.why: Sepsis is the body’s extreme response to infection and can lead to organ failure and death without quick treatment. It can start from infections in lungs, stomach, kidneys, bladder or even a small cut.
urgent_if: Not responding or confused or disoriented
Rapid breathing, shortness of breath or very fast heart rate
Fever with shivering or feeling very cold, clammy or sweaty skin
Extreme pain or discomfort

about.reply: Sepsis is your body's extreme, overactive response to an infection that can become life-threatening and lead to organ damage if not treated quickly.
about.next_step: Get medical care right away if you have an infection that is getting worse or you develop rapid breathing, confusion, fever with shivering or feeling very cold, clammy skin, or extreme pain or discomfort.
about.why: It is usually triggered by bacterial infections in the lungs, stomach, kidneys or bladder, and can start from a small cut or after surgery. People 65 or older, with chronic conditions like diabetes or kidney disease, weakened immunity, pregnancy, or children under one are more likely to develop it.
urgent_if: Rapid breathing and heart rate
Shortness of breath
Confusion or disorientation
Fever, shivering, or feeling very cold with clammy or sweaty skin

care.reply: Shingles is a painful rash caused by the varicella-zoster virus that stays in the body after chickenpox and can reactivate later, especially after age 50 or with a weaker immune system. Keep the rash covered with loose clothing, avoid direct contact with the blister fluid, and avoid close contact with pregnant people, newborns and anyone with a weakened immune system until the rash crusts.
care.next_step: See a doctor today, ideally within 72 hours of the rash appearing, to discuss care and pain relief. If the rash is near the eye, or there is fever, spreading redness, or the person is immunocompromised, seek care now.
care.why: Antiviral treatment is most helpful when started early, and covering the rash lowers the risk of passing chickenpox to someone who has never had it. The exact plan depends on age, health and how the rash looks.
urgent_if: rash near or in the eye with vision change
fever, confusion or feeling very unwell
rash spreading rapidly with severe pain

about.reply: Shingles is a painful rash caused by the varicella-zoster virus, the same virus that causes chickenpox. After chickenpox, the virus stays in your body and can reactivate later, most often as you get older or when your immune system is weakened.
about.next_step: See a doctor promptly if you notice a painful blistering rash on one side of the body, ideally within 2 to 3 days of onset.
about.why: Reactivation of the dormant chickenpox virus causes shingles, and risk rises with age over 50 and with weakened immunity. Early medical review matters because treatment is most helpful soon after the rash appears.

care.reply: Sinusitis means the air spaces around the nose are inflamed and mucus can’t drain well, which can cause facial pain, congestion, postnasal drip, cough, fever and fatigue. At home, saline nasal spray, warm compress on the face, steam inhalation and rest can help comfort, and pain relievers can be used as per label.
care.next_step: Get medical care today if fever lasts more than 3 days, symptoms are severe from the start, or symptoms last >10 days without improvement; otherwise see a doctor within 2 to 3 days if not better.
care.why: Acute sinusitis often starts like a cold and may become bacterial, while allergies and nasal blockage can also cause it. A health professional diagnoses it by symptoms and exam, sometimes with imaging, and treatment may include antibiotics, decongestants or pain relievers.
urgent_if: high fever with confusion
severe headache with neck stiffness
vision changes
swelling around eyes

about.reply: Sinusitis is inflammation of the hollow air spaces around your nose, which makes mucus drain poorly and causes pain, congestion and pressure. It is commonly caused by a cold turning into an infection, allergies, nasal swelling or blockage, and other nasal problems. See a doctor if symptoms last more than 10 days, are getting worse after initial improvement, are severe with high fever, or keep coming back.
about.next_step: If you have sinus symptoms that are not improving after 10 days, getting worse, or you have high fever, weakness or facial pain, book a check with your doctor within 2 to 3 days.
about.why: Sinusitis is diagnosed by symptoms and an exam of nose and face, sometimes with imaging. Treatments can include antibiotics, decongestants, pain relievers and supportive measures like saline sprays and heat, but the right choice depends on cause and duration.

care.reply: Sleep disorders are conditions that disturb normal sleep patterns and can affect energy, thinking and daily functioning. Poor quality or interrupted sleep is not just about hours in bed, it also matters which sleep stages you get.
care.next_step: Keep a regular sleep-wake time, limit screens and caffeine late in the day, and note when the sleep problem started and how it affects daytime functioning. See a doctor within 2 to 3 days if sleep problems last more than a few weeks, cause daytime sleepiness, or interfere with wo
care.why: Sleep is a natural process that helps restore energy and supports learning and memory. When sleep is often interrupted you may miss key non-REM and REM stages, which can affect physical and mental health.

about.reply: Sleep disorders are conditions that disturb your normal sleep patterns and quality, not just the number of hours you get. They can affect how you feel, think and function during the day because sleep helps restore energy, learning and memory.
about.next_step: Talk to a doctor if poor sleep lasts more than a few weeks, causes daytime sleepiness, or affects work, mood or safety.
about.why: Sleep involves cycles of non-REM and REM stages. If sleep is often interrupted you may miss key stages, which can affect physical and mental health.

care.reply: A sore throat is often from a cold, flu or irritation, and soothing care at home can help now. Keep them drinking fluids, rest, and use lozenges or warm salt-water gargles for comfort, and avoid aspirin in children.
care.next_step: If pain, fever or trouble swallowing is not better in 3 to 4 days, or if it started suddenly with fever and swollen tonsils, get a doctor check within 2 to 3 days.
care.why: Many sore throats are viral and improve with supportive care, but treatment depends on the cause such as strep throat, mononucleosis, allergies or smoking irritation. The report's own range and their doctor's plan come first.
urgent_if: trouble breathing or swallowing
throat swelling or drooling
fever over 39°C with rash or stiff neck
sore throat with vomiting blood

about.reply: A sore throat is pain or irritation in the pharynx, the tube that carries food to your esophagus and air to your windpipe and voice box. It is commonly caused by colds and flu, and also by allergies, smoking, mononucleosis, strep throat and tonsillitis. See a doctor if the pain is severe, lasts more than a few days, you have trouble breathing or swallowing, fever, rash, or swollen neck glands.
about.next_step: If sore throat is not better in 3 to 4 days, or you develop fever, trouble breathing or swallowing, see a doctor within 1 to 2 days.
about.why: The cause determines treatment, and most viral sore throats improve with fluids, lozenges and gargling, while bacterial causes may need medical care. The report's own range and your doctor's plan come first for any test.

care.reply: For a possible sprain or strain, rest the injured area now and protect it from further movement. Ice it, use gentle compression with a bandage, and keep the area raised if it is a limb, and follow the label for any pain medicine you already use.
care.next_step: Get medical care today if there is a lot of swelling, bruising, inability to move the joint or muscle, or pain that is not easing with rest and ice, and seek care within 2 to 3 days if it is not clearly improving.
care.why: Sprains are injured ligaments and strains are injured muscles or tendons, both often cause pain, swelling and trouble moving. Early rest, ice, compression and elevation help limit swelling, and a clinician can check for a more serious injury and guide safe recovery.
urgent_if: cannot move the joint or limb at all
severe swelling or deformity after injury
numbness or tingling in the area
pain that is rapidly worsening

about.reply: A sprain is a stretched or torn ligament that connects bones at a joint, and a strain is a stretched or torn muscle or tendon that connects muscle to bone. They are commonly caused by falling, twisting, getting hit, or pulling, with ankle and wrist sprains and back and hamstring strains being frequent.
about.next_step: See a doctor within 2 to 3 days if pain, swelling or trouble moving does not improve with rest, ice, compression and elevation, or if you cannot bear weight, the joint looks deformed, or there is numbness.
about.why: Sprains and strains share pain, swelling and limited movement, and initial care is usually rest, ice, compression and medicines, with later exercise or physical therapy as needed. The exact cause and severity can only be confirmed by an exam.

care.reply: Stress is the body’s normal alert response to a challenge or demand, and it can be short-term or long-term. For short-term stress, calming routines like slow breathing, regular sleep, gentle movement, and talking with someone you trust can help the body settle after the demand passes.
care.next_step: Try simple calming steps today and note if stress lasts for weeks or is interfering with sleep, work or daily life.
care.why: Stress hormones can raise blood pressure, heart rate and blood sugar to help you act quickly, but stress that lasts weeks or months can harm health. What is uncertain is how long it has lasted and how much it is affecting this person.

about.reply: Stress is your brain and body’s alert response to a challenge or demand, releasing hormones that raise blood pressure, heart rate and blood sugar to help you act quickly. It can be short-term, like a sudden scare or a deadline, or long-term when demands keep happening for weeks or months.
about.next_step: If stress lasts weeks or months, is getting worse, or is affecting sleep, mood, work or health, book a check with a doctor within the next few days.
about.why: Short-term stress can be helpful, but long-term stress can harm health because the body stays in fight-or-flight mode. The exact causes and impact vary by person, so a doctor can assess your situation.

care.reply: Call 112 now. A stroke is a medical emergency because brain cells can start to die within minutes without blood flow.
care.next_step: Call 112 immediately and do not give food or drink. Keep the person still and note when symptoms started.
care.why: Loss of blood flow to the brain can cause lasting brain damage, disability or death, and immediate treatment improves chances of recovery. The exact cause cannot be known without examination.
urgent_if: Face drooping on one side
Weak arm or leg on one side
Sudden strange or slurred speech
Sudden worst headache

about.reply: A stroke is when blood flow to part of the brain is lost, so brain cells stop getting oxygen and nutrients and can start to die within minutes. The most common cause is a blood clot blocking a brain vessel, called ischemic stroke, and the other main type is bleeding from a broken vessel, called hemorrhagic stroke. Call 112 right away if you think someone may be having a stroke, because immediate treatment can save life and improve recovery.
about.next_step: If you notice sudden face drooping, arm weakness, or strange or slurred speech, call 112 now and do not give food or drink.
about.why: Loss of blood flow quickly damages brain cells, which is why time matters. Risk is higher with high blood pressure, diabetes and heart conditions like atrial fibrillation.
urgent_if: Face drooping on one side
Weak arm or leg suddenly
Sudden strange or slurred speech
Sudden worst headache or confusion

care.reply: Thyroid diseases happen when the butterfly-shaped gland in the front of your neck makes too much or too little hormone, which can affect heart rate, weight, digestion, mood and energy use. Diagnosis is done by a health care provider with history, physical exam and thyroid tests, and treatment depends on the specific problem and symptoms.
care.next_step: Book a check-up with a doctor soon for proper testing and advice, and seek care sooner if symptoms are new, worsening or interfering with daily life.
care.why: Hormone levels need lab tests to know if they are high or low, and management varies by type and severity. The report's own range and the doctor's plan come first.

about.reply: Thyroid disease means your butterfly-shaped thyroid gland in the front of your neck makes too much or too little hormone, which affects breathing, heart rate, weight, digestion and mood. Common problems include goiter, hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism, nodules, thyroiditis and thyroid cancer.
about.why: The thyroid hormones control how your body uses energy and affect nearly every organ. Diagnosis is usually by history, physical exam and thyroid tests, and treatment depends on the specific problem and symptoms.

about.reply: Thyroid tests are blood and imaging tests that check how well your thyroid gland in the front of your neck is making hormones that control energy use, heart rate, breathing, digestion, weight and mood.
about.why: TSH is usually the first blood test, with T3 and T4 measuring thyroid hormones and antibody tests helping with autoimmune causes. Imaging like ultrasound or thyroid scan can show size, shape and nodules.

care.reply: Tooth disorders cover many problems like decay, abscess, impacted teeth, misalignment or injury, and they can cause tooth pain, abnormal color or shape, or worn-down teeth. At home keep the area clean with gentle brushing and flossing, avoid very hot, cold, hard or sugary foods, and do not try to treat an infection yourself.
care.next_step: Book a dentist check within 2 to 3 days for pain, sensitivity, visible damage, or a change in color/shape; sooner if symptoms are worsening.
care.why: Causes vary from poor care to injury or being born with the problem, and symptoms differ by the specific issue. A dentist can examine the teeth and decide what care is needed.
urgent_if: swelling in face or neck spreading quickly
fever with tooth pain
trouble breathing or swallowing
pus discharge with severe pain

about.reply: Tooth disorders are problems that affect your teeth, such as decay, infection, injury or teeth that are misaligned or did not come in properly. They can make eating, speaking and smiling uncomfortable or difficult.
about.next_step: See a dentist within 2 to 3 days for tooth pain, a visible broken or chipped tooth, swelling in the gum or face, or a bad taste or pus.
about.why: Teeth are made of enamel, dentin, cementum and a soft pulp with nerves and blood vessels. Causes vary from poor oral care and tooth decay to injury or being born with the problem.

care.reply: Tuberculosis is a bacterial infection that usually affects the lungs and can spread through the air when someone with active TB coughs, sneezes, talks or sings. Because it can spread in households, the person who may have TB needs a medical evaluation promptly and close contacts should avoid sharing airspace until they are assessed.
care.next_step: Arrange a doctor visit today for evaluation and testing, and keep the person from close indoor contact with others until they are seen.
care.why: TB germs spread person to person through the air, not by touching or sharing dishes, and active TB can be treated with antibiotics but needs proper diagnosis and treatment. It is not possible to know from a description whether this is latent infection or active disease.
urgent_if: coughing up blood
trouble breathing or chest pain
high fever with night sweats that is not improving
confusion or very weak and unable to care for self

about.reply: Tuberculosis is a bacterial infection, usually in the lungs, that can also affect kidneys, spine and brain. It spreads through the air when someone with active TB in the throat or lungs coughs, sneezes, talks or sings, and you breathe in the germs. See a doctor promptly if you have a cough lasting more than 2-3 weeks, fever, night sweats, weight loss, or coughing up blood.
about.next_step: If you have a persistent cough, fever, night sweats or weight loss, book a doctor visit within 2 to 3 days.
about.why: TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and can be latent or active disease. Active TB can almost always be cured with antibiotics if treated properly, but it can be fatal if not treated.

about.reply: Urinalysis is a simple lab test that checks your urine for color, clarity, odor, acidity and substances that are not normally there, such as blood, protein, glucose, ketones, bilirubin, cells, crystals, casts and germs.
about.why: It is commonly done to check for urinary tract infection, kidney problems or diabetes, and also during checkups, hospital admission, before surgery or in pregnancy to monitor conditions and treatments. The report’s own reference ranges and your doctor’s plan come first.

care.reply: A urinary tract infection is an infection in the urinary system that can cause burning with urination, frequent urge to pass urine, lower belly pressure, cloudy or bad-smelling urine, fever, tiredness or shakiness, and pain in the back or side below the ribs. It is usually confirmed with a urine test and treated with antibiotics prescribed by a doctor.
care.next_step: Have the person seen a doctor today for a urine test and advice; do not start antibiotics on your own.
care.why: Only a doctor can confirm a UTI with a test and choose the right antibiotic. Symptoms can overlap with other problems and some UTIs can spread to the kidneys.
urgent_if: Fever with shaking or chills
Pain in back or side below ribs
Confusion, drowsiness or not responding
Unable to pass urine or vomiting

about.reply: A urinary tract infection is an infection in the body's drainage system for urine, which includes the kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra. It often happens when bacteria get into the urethra and grow in the bladder or higher up, and it is more common in women and in people with diabetes or a tube to drain the bladder.
about.next_step: See a doctor promptly if you have burning with urination, frequent urge to urinate, lower belly pressure, cloudy or bad-smelling urine, fever, tiredness or back/side pain below the ribs.
about.why: UTIs are the second most common infection and are usually confirmed with a urine test and treated with antibiotics. The exact cause for a person can only be known after examination and testing.

care.reply: Vaginal problems are common and can show up as itching, burning, pain, abnormal bleeding or discharge. A doctor needs to examine the person and, if needed, do tests to find the cause, because treatment depends on the cause.
care.next_step: Book a clinic visit within 2 to 3 days for an exam, and go sooner if symptoms are new, worsening, or distressing.
care.why: Vaginitis and other vaginal conditions have overlapping symptoms and different causes such as infections, irritation or other problems. Only an in-person exam can identify the cause and guide safe care.
urgent_if: heavy or ongoing vaginal bleeding
severe pelvic or abdominal pain
fever with vaginal discharge or pain
foul-smelling discharge with fever or feeling very unwell

about.reply: Vaginal diseases are problems that affect the vagina and vulva, and they are a common reason women see a doctor. They often show up as itching, burning, pain, abnormal bleeding or unusual discharge. One common type is vaginitis, an inflammation of the vagina, and other causes can include infections, sexually transmitted infections, and rarely cancers.
about.next_step: See a doctor within 2 to 3 days if you have itching, burning, pain, abnormal bleeding or unusual discharge that does not go away, or sooner if symptoms are new or worsening.
about.why: Symptoms overlap between many causes, so treatment depends on finding the cause. A clinician can examine you and, if needed, do tests to know what is causing it.

about.reply: Vitamin D is a vitamin your body needs to absorb calcium for strong bones and to help nerves, muscles and immune system work normally. You can get it from sunlight on skin, from fortified foods like milk and cereal, and from supplements; very few foods naturally have it.
about.why: It helps your body absorb calcium which builds bone, and supports nerve, muscle and immune function. A lack can lead to bone problems such as osteoporosis or rickets over time.

about.reply: Vitamins are natural substances your body needs in small amounts to grow, develop and stay healthy, and you usually get them from a balanced variety of foods. Your body can make some vitamins like D and K, but most must come from food, and people on a vegetarian diet may need a B12 supplement.
about.why: Each vitamin has specific jobs and low levels can lead to health problems, for example low vitamin C can contribute to anemia and low vitamin A can cause night blindness. High doses of some vitamins can also cause problems, so supplements should be discussed with a health care provider first.

care.reply: For a wound, first check how bad it is. Minor cuts, scrapes and scratches usually need gentle cleaning with clean water, keeping the area covered and watching for signs of infection. Serious or dirty wounds need prompt care.
care.next_step: Clean a minor wound now with clean running water and cover it with a clean dressing; get medical care today if the wound is deep, bleeding does not stop, cannot be closed, has dirt you cannot remove, or looks infected.
care.why: Wounds break the skin and can let germs in. Minor wounds often heal with basic cleaning, but deep, heavily bleeding or contaminated wounds may need first aid followed by a doctor's visit.
urgent_if: heavy bleeding that does not stop with firm pressure
wound is deep, gaping or you cannot close it
signs of infection such as increasing redness, warmth, swelling or pus
animal bite or puncture wound

about.reply: A wound is an injury that breaks the skin or other body tissues, such as cuts, scrapes, scratches and punctures. Injuries are a broad term for damage to the body from accidents, falls, hits, weapons and more, and can range from minor to life-threatening.
about.why: Wounds are a type of injury, and injuries commonly happen at work or play, indoors or outdoors, while driving or walking. Minor wounds usually aren't serious but need cleaning.

care.reply: Acne is a common skin condition where hair follicles clog and form pimples, often on the face, neck, back, chest and shoulders. Gentle skin care helps now: clean skin gently, try not to touch or pick it, and avoid sun exposure. Treatments exist as medicines and creams, and a doctor can advise which is suitable.
care.next_step: Start gentle skin care today and book a doctor visit within 2 to 3 days if pimples are painful, widespread, causing scars, or not improving with basic care.
care.why: Hormone changes probably play a role and stress can make acne worse, but dirt, chocolate and greasy foods are myths with little evidence for most people. The report's own range and a doctor's plan come first for personal care.

about.reply: Acne is a common skin condition that causes pimples when hair follicles under the skin get clogged. It most often appears on the face, neck, back, chest and shoulders and is common in teenagers and young adults. Hormone changes are thought to play a role, but dirty skin, chocolate, greasy foods and stress do not cause it, though stress can make it worse.
about.next_step: See a doctor if acne is painful, leaves scars, is spreading quickly, or is not improving with gentle skin care.
about.why: Clogged follicles lead to pimples and blackheads. Hormone changes during teenage years and pregnancy probably contribute, but food and dirt are myths. Gentle cleaning and avoiding picking helps, and treatments exist when needed.

care.reply: Bad breath is often from bacteria building up in the mouth from not brushing and flossing regularly, dry mouth, gum disease or cavities, foods like onion and garlic, smoking, or sinus/nose problems. Good daily dental habits, staying hydrated and avoiding strong-smelling foods and smoking usually help freshen breath now.
care.next_step: Start regular brushing twice daily with floss, drink water through the day, and avoid tobacco and strong odor foods. If bad breath lasts more than 2 to 3 weeks despite good oral care, or comes with mouth pain, swelling, fever, or a change in taste, book a dentist or doctor within
care.why: Bacteria between teeth and gum problems are common causes of odor, and mouthwashes or mints can temporarily mask it. Persistent odor can signal gum disease, dry mouth, sinus issues or a disease or medicine effect that needs treatment.

about.reply: Bad breath is a bad smell from the mouth, usually from bacteria building up on the tongue, teeth and gums. It commonly happens with poor brushing and flossing, dry mouth, gum disease or cavities, eating strong foods like onion or garlic, smoking, sinus or nose problems, and some diseases or medicines.
about.next_step: If bad breath lasts more than a few days despite regular brushing, flossing and staying hydrated, book a dental check within 2 to 3 days.
about.why: Bacteria in the mouth produce odor, and mouth problems, foods, smoking and some health conditions can make it worse. The report's own range and your doctor's plan come first for personal advice.

care.reply: Bladder diseases cover many different problems such as infection, overactive bladder, incontinence and bladder pain, and they need a doctor to find the cause with urine tests and examination.
care.next_step: Book a doctor visit within 2 to 3 days for assessment, and go sooner if any urgent signs appear.
care.why: The cause decides care, and tests like urine tests and bladder examination are used to diagnose. Without knowing which problem it is, home care alone is not enough.
urgent_if: fever with burning or painful urination
blood in urine
unable to pass urine or severe lower abdominal pain
confusion or drowsiness in an older adult

about.reply: Bladder diseases are problems with the hollow organ in your lower abdomen that stores urine before you pass it out. Common types include cystitis from infection, loss of bladder control, overactive bladder that squeezes at the wrong time, and chronic bladder pain with frequent urgent urination.
about.next_step: See a doctor within 2 to 3 days if you have burning with urination, frequent urgent need to pass urine, blood in urine, or pain in the lower abdomen or pelvis.
about.why: The bladder can be affected by infection, muscle control problems and chronic inflammation. The report's own range and your doctor's plan come first for diagnosis and treatment.

care.reply: COVID-19 is an illness caused by SARS-CoV-2 that spreads through droplets and very small particles when an infected person breathes out. At home the usual first steps are to isolate the person who is sick, wear a well-fitting mask around them, wash hands often, and monitor symptoms like fever, cough, sore throat, tiredness and loss of taste or smell.
care.next_step: Keep the person at home and separate from others, and call a doctor today for guidance on testing, isolation length and care at home. Seek care sooner if symptoms worsen or any urgent signs appear.
care.why: Isolation and basic hygiene reduce spread to family members. A doctor can confirm the situation, advise on testing and when it is safe to be around others, and check for risk factors.
urgent_if: trouble breathing or shortness of breath
chest pain or pressure
confusion or difficulty waking
blue lips or face

about.reply: COVID-19 is an illness caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus. It is commonly caused by breathing in droplets and very small particles with the virus that an infected person breathes out.
about.next_step: See a doctor promptly for fever, cough, trouble breathing, loss of taste or smell, or if you are at higher risk and feel unwell.
about.why: The virus spreads through respiratory droplets and particles from an infected person. Symptoms and severity vary, so medical advice is needed for personal risk and care.

care.reply: Canker sores are small painful mouth ulcers with a red edge and gray center that are not contagious and often heal on their own. For now keep the mouth gentle, avoid hot, spicy or acidic foods, and use a simple salt-water rinse or over-the-counter mouth rinse for comfort if tolerated.
care.next_step: See a doctor within 2 to 3 days if the sore is not improving, is very large or painful, or if new sores keep coming back.
care.why: Most canker sores resolve by themselves in about 1 to 2 weeks and pain relief and avoiding irritants usually helps. The cause is often unknown and can be triggered by stress, certain foods, vitamin deficiencies or hormonal changes.

about.reply: Canker sores are small, round painful ulcers inside the mouth, often on the cheek, under the tongue or throat, with a red edge and gray center. They are not contagious and are different from cold sores caused by herpes. Common triggers include stress, certain foods, minor injury, lack of vitamins and minerals, hormonal changes and sometimes a viral infection, though the cause is often unknown.
about.why: They usually heal on their own in most cases and pain can be eased by avoiding hot, spicy foods and using over-the-counter rinses or creams. See a doctor if a sore lasts more than 2 weeks, keeps coming back, is very large or painful, or you have trouble eating or drinking.

care.reply: Cannabis is a plant product that contains chemicals like THC which can change how a person feels, thinks and senses, and CBD which does not cause a high. Effects vary with amount used, THC level, how it is taken, other medicines and health conditions, and can include altered mood, senses and sense of time while high.
care.next_step: Keep the person safe and calm, do not leave them alone, and avoid giving food, drink or medicines unless advised by a doctor. If you are worried about their current state, call 112 for guidance today.
care.why: Effects are short-term and can be different for each person, and the evidence describes general effects not a diagnosis for this person. What is safe to do next depends on how they are right now.
urgent_if: Not breathing normally or trouble breathing
Unresponsive, cannot be woken or is confused and getting worse
Chest pain or pressure
Severe vomiting or repeated vomiting

about.reply: Cannabis is the dried leaves, flowers and resin from the cannabis plant, often called marijuana. It contains chemicals called cannabinoids, mainly THC which causes a high, and CBD which does not cause a high, and it is used by smoking, vaping, eating as edibles, tinctures or topicals.
about.why: It is a plant product, not an illness you catch, so it does not have a cause in the medical sense. Effects vary with amount, THC level, how it is taken and your health.

care.reply: Carpal tunnel syndrome is a common problem where the median nerve in the wrist gets squeezed, often causing numbness, tingling, weakness or pain in the wrist and hand, especially the thumb and first three fingers. At home, general comfort measures are to avoid repeated wrist bending, take short breaks from repetitive hand work, and keep the wrist in a neutral position; do not start or stop any medicine on your own.
care.next_step: Book a check with a doctor within 2 to 3 days for assessment and guidance, sooner if symptoms are new or worsening.
care.why: Symptoms come from pressure on the median nerve in the narrow carpal tunnel, often from swelling of tendons or underlying conditions like diabetes or rheumatoid arthritis. The right plan depends on exam and history, so a clinician needs to decide what is safe for this person.

about.reply: Carpal tunnel syndrome is numbness, tingling, weakness or pain in the wrist and hand caused by the median nerve being squeezed in the narrow carpal tunnel at the wrist.
about.next_step: See a doctor if the numbness, tingling or pain lasts more than a few days, gets worse, wakes you at night, or makes it hard to grip or do daily tasks.
about.why: The median nerve runs through the carpal tunnel with tendons to the hand. Swelling or irritation of those tendons can press on the nerve and reduce feeling and thumb movement. Causes are often a mix of wrist injury, swelling and health conditions like diabetes or rheumatoid arthritis.

care.reply: Corns and calluses are thickened skin from repeated pressure or friction, often on feet where bones rub against shoes, with corns more common on tops or sides of toes and calluses on soles, hands or other rubbed areas. At home you can reduce pressure by wearing shoes that fit better, using non-medicated pads, and while bathing gently rub the area with a washcloth or pumice stone; do not try to shave or cut them off to avoid infection.
care.next_step: Try better-fitting shoes and non-medicated pads now, and keep the skin clean and dry; see a doctor within 2 to 3 days if the area is painful, red, warm, swollen, has drainage, or is not improving with gentle care.
care.why: Pressure and friction cause the skin to thicken as protection, and reducing that pressure is the main way to help it improve. Cutting or shaving can introduce infection, which is why medical review is important, especially with diabetes or circulation problems.

about.reply: Corns and calluses are thickened areas of skin caused by repeated pressure or friction. Corns usually form on the tops or sides of toes, and calluses often form on the soles of feet, and can also appear on hands where skin is rubbed or pressed.
about.why: Pressure or friction makes the skin build up to protect itself. The location and cause are typical, but individual skin and health factors can change what is safe to do.

care.reply: Drinking water needs depend on your size, activity level and weather, and in many places the supply is treated to be safe. Your water supplier must give you an annual report on where the water comes from and what contaminants are in it.
care.why: Water quality can vary by place because it depends on source water and treatment. The report from your supplier is the best place to check for your area.

about.reply: Drinking water is the water you drink from taps, wells or bottles. It comes from surface water like rivers, lakes and reservoirs and from groundwater underground, and is usually treated to make it safe.
about.why: The evidence describes drinking water as a supply that varies by source and treatment, not as a medical condition with causes.

care.reply: Edema means swelling from fluid in body tissues, often in feet, ankles and legs, and it can be caused by many general things such as too much salt, heart, kidney or liver problems, pregnancy, medicines, or long standing or walking in warm weather.
care.next_step: Have the person checked by a doctor within the next 2 to 3 days for an exam and to find the cause, and sooner today if swelling is new, sudden, or getting worse.
care.why: Edema is a sign, not a diagnosis, and the right care depends on the underlying cause. General measures like leg raising, limiting salt and support stockings are sometimes suggested by a provider, but they should be guided by a doctor.
urgent_if: Trouble breathing or swelling of face, lips or tongue
Sudden swelling on one side of the body
Chest pain or pressure
Very rapid weight gain with swelling

about.reply: Edema is swelling caused by extra fluid building up in your body’s tissues, most often in the feet, ankles and legs.
about.why: It happens when fluid leaks into tissues and is not drained away. Common contributors include too much salt, sunburn, heart failure, kidney disease, liver problems from cirrhosis, pregnancy, lymph node problems after mastectomy, some medicines, and prolonged standing or walking in warm weather.

care.reply: Eye diseases are many and some have no early symptoms, so a regular comprehensive dilated eye exam is the safest way to check eyes that feel healthy. Do not try to diagnose at home; an eye care provider needs to look at the eyes directly.
care.next_step: Book a routine eye exam soon, and seek care today if there is sudden vision change, eye pain, redness with discharge, or injury.
care.why: Conditions like cataract, glaucoma, retinal and macular problems, and diabetic eye disease can be silent early on and may lead to permanent vision loss if missed. Early detection can help slow or prevent loss.
urgent_if: sudden loss of vision or curtain over vision
severe eye pain or redness with discharge
chemical splash or eye injury
swelling of eyelid with fever

about.reply: Eye diseases are problems that can affect how your eyes see or stay healthy, and some can cause permanent vision loss even if your eyes feel fine. Common types include cataracts, glaucoma from high fluid pressure, macular degeneration, diabetic eye problems, retinal disorders and pink eye conjunctivitis.
about.next_step: Book a comprehensive dilated eye exam with an eye care provider for a baseline check, and sooner if you notice vision changes.
about.why: Many eye conditions have no early symptoms, so regular exams help find them early when treatment can slow or prevent vision loss. Age, diabetes and long-standing high eye pressure are common risk factors.

care.reply: Foot health is kept with regular checks and gentle daily care. Examine your feet regularly, wear comfortable shoes that fit, wash feet daily with soap and lukewarm water, and trim toenails straight across and not too short.
care.next_step: Start daily foot checks and comfortable shoes now, and talk to a doctor if any foot problem is present or does not improve.
care.why: Feet carry weight and involve bones, muscles, tendons and ligaments, so regular care helps prevent problems. Foot changes can also reflect overall health, so a doctor should be involved when problems arise.

about.reply: Foot health means keeping the bones, muscles, tendons and ligaments in your feet working well and caring for the skin and nails, because your feet carry your body weight with every step. Common problems come from ill-fitting shoes, poor daily care, and underlying conditions that can show up in the feet.
about.why: Feet are a complex network that bears weight, so wear, pressure and circulation issues can cause pain or changes. Foot changes can also be clues to overall health like arthritis, diabetes, kidney, heart or blood pressure problems.

care.reply: Foot problems are common because each foot has many bones, joints and soft tissues, and things like ill-fitting shoes, aging and being overweight can increase the risk. For now keep the foot clean and dry, avoid tight or hard shoes, and do not try to cut corns, calluses or warts at home.
care.next_step: If there is pain, redness, swelling, warmth, open skin, a wound that is not healing, or walking is difficult, have a doctor check it within 2 to 3 days; see a doctor sooner if it is getting worse.
care.why: Many foot issues are linked to pressure and friction from shoes and general wear, but only an in-person check can tell what is causing this person’s problem and whether treatment is needed.
urgent_if: fever with a red hot swollen foot
sudden inability to bear weight
rapidly spreading redness or pus
open wound with heavy bleeding

about.reply: Foot injuries and disorders are problems with the bones, joints, tendons, muscles and ligaments in your feet. Common examples are bunions, corns and calluses, plantar warts, and fallen arches or flat feet.
about.next_step: See a doctor within 2 to 3 days if you have ongoing foot pain, swelling, redness, a bump that keeps growing, or trouble walking.
about.why: Your feet have 26 bones, 33 joints and over 100 tendons, muscles and ligaments, so many things can go wrong. Ill-fitting shoes, aging and being overweight are common contributors.

care.reply: Glaucoma is a group of eye diseases that can damage the optic nerve and lead to vision loss, often with no early symptoms. Regular eye exams by an eye care provider can check for it and treatments that lower eye pressure help slow the disease.
care.next_step: Book an eye care provider appointment soon for a dilated eye exam and follow their plan for monitoring and treatment.
care.why: The most common type is open-angle glaucoma where fluid pressure inside the eye slowly rises and can damage the optic nerve. Pressure tolerance varies by person, so a provider needs to check what is normal for them.
urgent_if: sudden eye pain or headache
sudden vision loss or seeing halos around lights
red eye with nausea or vomiting

about.reply: Glaucoma is a group of eye diseases that damage the optic nerve and can lead to vision loss, often starting with loss of side or peripheral vision. The most common type is open-angle glaucoma, which usually happens when fluid pressure inside the eye slowly rises and harms the optic nerve, though some people get it with normal pressure.
about.next_step: Book a regular dilated eye exam with an eye care provider for screening, and see a doctor sooner if you notice gradual loss of side vision, blurred vision, eye pain or halos around lights.
about.why: Pressure-related damage to the optic nerve is the usual mechanism, but the amount of pressure each person can tolerate varies and many people have no early symptoms.

care.reply: Gum disease ranges from mild gum inflammation called gingivitis, which can be reversed with daily brushing and flossing and regular dental cleanings, to more serious periodontitis that can damage the bone and tissue supporting teeth. At home, keep gentle twice-daily brushing and daily flossing, avoid smoking, and book a dental check soon so a dentist or hygienist can assess the gums and clean them properly.
care.next_step: Book a dental check within the next 2 to 3 days for an exam and professional cleaning, and keep up gentle brushing and flossing until then.
care.why: Gingivitis can often be reversed with good daily care and professional cleaning, but untreated inflammation can progress to periodontitis with gum recession, pockets and bone loss. Only a dentist who examines the person can tell how far it has gone and what care is needed.

about.reply: Gum disease is an infection of the gums that starts as gum inflammation called gingivitis and can progress to periodontitis, where the gums pull away from teeth and the supporting bone and tissue can be damaged.
about.next_step: Book a dental check within the next 1 to 2 weeks if your gums bleed when brushing or flossing, look red and swollen, or you notice bad breath that does not go away.
about.why: Gingivitis is mild and can often be reversed with daily brushing and flossing and regular professional cleanings, but untreated gingivitis can lead to periodontitis which can destroy bone and lead to tooth loss.

care.reply: H1N1 flu is a contagious respiratory infection with symptoms like fever, cough, sore throat, body aches, headache, chills and fatigue, similar to regular flu. At home focus on rest, fluids, fever comfort measures, and strict hygiene to limit spread to others.
care.next_step: Keep the person home and away from close contact with others, and call a doctor today for assessment and to discuss whether antiviral medicine is appropriate, especially if they are high risk or symptoms are worsening.
care.why: Antivirals can help prevent or treat swine flu but are most useful when started early, and hygiene measures reduce spread of respiratory germs. The exact need for testing and treatment depends on the person’s age, health conditions and how sick they are.
urgent_if: trouble breathing or wheezing
chest pain or pressure
confusion or drowsiness
fever not coming down or getting worse

about.reply: H1N1 flu, also called swine flu, is a flu infection caused by an influenza virus that normally infects pigs but can infect people and spread from person to person. It causes symptoms similar to regular flu such as fever, cough, sore throat, body aches, headache, chills and fatigue.
about.next_step: If you develop fever with cough or body aches, contact a doctor within 1 to 2 days for advice; seek care sooner if breathing is hard or symptoms worsen quickly.
about.why: The virus is contagious and spreads through coughs, sneezes and hands. Antiviral medicines and vaccine exist, and prevention relies on hand washing, covering coughs and staying home when sick.
urgent_if: trouble breathing or wheezing
chest pain or pressure
confusion or drowsiness
fever not improving after 3 days

care.reply: Losing up to about 100 hairs from the scalp each day is normal and hairs often grow back, but ongoing or patchy hair loss is worth checking.
care.next_step: Book a primary care check within 2 to 3 days if the loss is sudden, patchy, with scalp redness, scaling or pain, or if there are other symptoms like fatigue, weight change or fever; otherwise book a routine check within 2 to 3 weeks to find the cause.
care.why: Hair loss can be normal shedding or related to thyroid problems, diabetes, lupus, medicines, chemotherapy, stress, low protein or poor nutrition. Treatment depends on the cause, and treating an underlying cause can help hair regrow.

about.reply: Hair loss is losing more hair than the normal up to about 100 scalp hairs a day, and in most people those hairs grow back. It commonly happens with ageing, family history, stress, poor nutrition or a low protein diet, and can also be linked to thyroid problems, diabetes, lupus, certain medicines or chemotherapy.
about.next_step: See a doctor within 2 to 3 days if hair loss is sudden, patchy, comes with scalp redness, scaling or pain, or if you notice other symptoms like fatigue or weight change.
about.why: Hair shedding is normal, but ongoing loss often reflects an underlying cause. Treating the cause can help, and medicines or hair restoration are options depending on the reason.

care.reply: Hand problems can make daily tasks hard, so keep the hand protected and avoid using it for heavy or repetitive work until it is checked. Rest, gentle support with a soft bandage or splint if it is painful, and avoid forcing movement can help now.
care.next_step: Have the person seen a doctor within 2 to 3 days for assessment, or sooner if pain, swelling or function is getting worse.
care.why: Hand injuries and disorders range from nerve compression like carpal tunnel to fractures, dislocations, tendon irritation and arthritis, and only an exam can tell which is present and what care is needed.
urgent_if: heavy bleeding from a hand wound
a visible deformity or bone sticking out
cannot move fingers or the hand is numb and cold
severe pain after a fall or injury

about.reply: Hand injuries and disorders are problems that affect the hands, fingers and thumb and can make regular activities difficult. Common examples are carpal tunnel syndrome from nerve compression at the wrist, fractures, ruptured ligaments and dislocations, osteoarthritis wear-and-tear arthritis that can cause deformity, tendinitis from irritated tendons, and injuries to fingers and thumb.
about.next_step: See a doctor promptly if you have persistent pain, numbness, swelling, loss of movement, a visible deformity, or an injury that does not improve in a few days.
about.why: These conditions involve nerves, bones, ligaments, tendons and joints, and the evidence lists carpal tunnel syndrome, fractures, ruptured ligaments, dislocations, osteoarthritis and tendinitis as common hand problems.

care.reply: Hearing problems can often be helped, and a doctor can check the cause and discuss options like hearing aids, training or treatment. Do not try to clean the ear canal yourself.
care.next_step: Book a hearing check with a doctor within the next 2 to 3 days, sooner if the loss is sudden or one-sided.
care.why: Hearing loss can be from inner ear or nerve damage which is often permanent, or from blockage like earwax, fluid or eardrum injury which can sometimes be reversed. Untreated problems can get worse over time.

about.reply: Hearing disorders make it hard to hear well enough to enjoy talking with friends or family, while deafness can keep you from hearing sound at all. Hearing loss can be from inner ear or nerve damage which is often permanent, or from sound not reaching the inner ear due to earwax, fluid or eardrum problems which can sometimes be reversed.
about.next_step: If you have trouble hearing, book a hearing check with a doctor or ENT soon, ideally within 2 to 3 days.
about.why: Common causes include heredity, ear infections and meningitis, trauma, certain medicines, long-term loud noise exposure and aging. Untreated hearing problems can get worse over time.

care.reply: A hernia is when part of an internal organ or tissue bulges through a weak area of muscle, most often in the abdomen such as groin or around the belly button. At home avoid heavy lifting, straining, coughing without support and keep the area comfortable while you arrange medical review.
care.next_step: Get a doctor to examine the bulge within the next few days for advice on care and whether repair is needed.
care.why: Hernias often need clinical exam to confirm type and whether it can be reduced, and surgery is usually the treatment to repair the muscle opening. Untreated hernias can cause pain and health problems.
urgent_if: Sudden severe pain in the bulge
Bulge becomes hard, red, very tender or cannot be pushed back
Vomiting, fever or belly pain
Trouble passing stool or gas

about.reply: A hernia is when part of an internal organ or tissue bulges through a weak area of muscle, most often in the abdomen. It commonly happens with muscle weakness plus straining such as heavy lifting, and some people are born with weaker abdominal muscles.
about.why: Hernias are common in men, women and children and can be inguinal in the groin, umbilical around the belly button, incisional through a scar, or hiatal where the stomach moves up into the chest. Untreated hernias can cause pain and health problems and treatment is usually surgery to repair the muscle opening.

care.reply: Hip pain can come from strains, bursitis, overuse, a fall or from joint problems like osteoarthritis and osteoporosis. For now keep the person comfortable, avoid putting weight on the painful hip and do gentle rest, and do not try to force movement.
care.next_step: Get a doctor seen today if there is severe pain, inability to bear weight, a visible deformity, or pain after a fall or injury; otherwise book a check within 2 to 3 days if pain limits daily activities.
care.why: Hips are stable ball-and-socket joints that usually need great force to injure, but sports, running, overuse or falls can cause strains, bursitis, dislocations or fractures. Osteoarthritis and osteoporosis are common causes of hip pain and limited motion in older people.
urgent_if: Not able to move the leg or bear weight
Visible deformity or leg looks shortened or turned
Severe pain after a fall or injury
Fever with hip pain

about.reply: Your hip is a ball-and-socket joint where the thigh bone meets the pelvis, which is very stable and allows wide motion. Hip injuries and disorders are problems to that joint, such as strains, bursitis, dislocations and fractures from force, and conditions like osteoarthritis, osteoporosis and hip dysplasia that make the hip painful or loose.
about.next_step: See a doctor promptly for new hip pain after a fall or injury, pain that limits walking, or pain that does not improve with rest in a few days.
about.why: Forceful events like sports, running, overuse or falls can injure the hip, and age-related diseases can weaken bone or change joint shape. The exact cause for a person needs an exam and history.

care.reply: Infertility means not becoming pregnant after frequent unprotected sex for one year or longer, or after six months if you are age 35 or older. It also includes being able to get pregnant but having repeated miscarriage or stillbirth. It can affect men and women and sometimes both partners contribute.
care.next_step: Book an appointment with a doctor in the next 2 to 3 weeks to discuss timing of intercourse, menstrual history and general health, and to plan initial checks.
care.why: A doctor can take a detailed history for both partners and decide which basic tests are appropriate. The timing for seeking care is shorter at age 35 or older because fertility declines with age.

about.reply: Infertility means not becoming pregnant after having frequent unprotected sex for one year or longer, or after six months if you are age 35 or older. It also includes being able to get pregnant but having repeated miscarriage or stillbirth. It is common and can affect one or both partners, and sometimes no clear cause is found.
about.next_step: If you have been trying for 12 months without pregnancy, or 6 months if you are 35 or older, book a check with your doctor soon to discuss testing and options.
about.why: The time frames come from standard definitions, and causes vary by person. A doctor can check ovulation, fallopian tubes, uterus, sperm count and movement, hormones and lifestyle factors.

care.reply: Most insect bites and stings cause only local pain or itching and can be cared for at home with gentle cleaning and cool compresses. Watch for signs of a severe allergic reaction or infection and get care promptly if they appear.
care.next_step: Clean the bite or sting gently with soap and water, apply a cool compress for discomfort, and watch for worsening redness, swelling or systemic symptoms for the next 24 hours.
care.why: Bee, wasp, hornet stings and fire ant bites usually hurt, while mosquito and flea bites usually itch. Insects can also spread diseases, and severe allergic reactions can occur.
urgent_if: trouble breathing or wheezing
swelling of lips, tongue or throat
widespread hives with dizziness or faintness
rapidly spreading redness, warmth, pus or fever

about.reply: Insect bites and stings are skin injuries from insects biting to feed or defending themselves with a sting. Common causes are mosquitoes and fleas that bite for blood and itch, and bees, wasps, hornets and fire ants that sting and usually hurt. See a doctor if the area becomes very red, warm, swollen or painful, shows signs of infection, you have a severe allergic reaction, or you know you are at risk for insect-spread diseases after travel.
about.why: The report's own range and your doctor's plan come first for personal advice.

care.reply: Irritable bowel syndrome is a common bowel problem that causes abdominal cramping, bloating and changes in bowel habits, but it does not harm the intestines.
care.next_step: Book a doctor visit soon for assessment and a personal plan for diet, stress management and medicines; seek care today if any red flag signs appear.
care.why: There is no specific test for IBS and doctors usually run tests to rule out other diseases first. Most people can control symptoms with diet, stress management, probiotics and medicine guided by a doctor.
urgent_if: blood in stool
unexplained weight loss
fever with abdominal pain
persistent vomiting

about.reply: Irritable Bowel Syndrome is a common problem of the large intestine that causes abdominal cramping, bloating and changes in bowel habits like constipation, diarrhea or alternating between them. It causes discomfort but does not harm the intestines, and it is more common in women and people under 45.
about.next_step: See a doctor if you have persistent abdominal pain with bowel changes, blood in stool, unexplained weight loss, fever, or symptoms that are new after age 50.
about.why: The exact cause is not known. Diagnosis is by ruling out other diseases with tests, and symptoms are often managed with diet, stress management, probiotics and medicine.

care.reply: Lactose intolerance means the body has trouble digesting lactose, the sugar in milk and milk foods, which can cause stomach upset, gas, bloating and diarrhea after dairy.
care.next_step: Try reducing milk and milk foods for a few days and note symptoms, and book a check with a doctor within 2 to 3 days if symptoms are frequent or you are unsure what to avoid.
care.why: Symptoms come from undigested lactose fermenting in the gut. A doctor can confirm with blood, breath or stool tests and advise on diet and calcium needs.

about.reply: Lactose intolerance means your body makes too little lactase, the enzyme needed to digest lactose, the sugar in milk and milk foods. After eating those foods you may get stomach upset, gas, bloating or diarrhea.
about.next_step: See a doctor if stomach symptoms are new, frequent, or interfere with daily life, or if you are unsure about calcium intake.
about.why: Lactose needs lactase to be broken down; without enough, undigested lactose causes gas and loose motions. Tests like blood, breath or stool can confirm it, and the report's own range and doctor's plan come first.

care.reply: Leg injuries can range from sprains and strains to fractures and joint problems, and care depends on how bad the injury is and whether the person can move or bear weight safely. For now keep the leg protected, avoid putting weight on it, and watch for increasing pain, swelling or bruising.
care.next_step: Get a same-day medical check if there is visible deformity, inability to bear weight, rapid swelling, numbness, or pain that is not easing with rest; otherwise see a doctor within 2 to 3 days for persistent pain or limited motion.
care.why: Sprains, strains, dislocations and fractures can affect the whole leg or just foot, ankle, knee or hip, and some leg problems come from diseases like knee osteoarthritis or vein problems. The report's own range and a clinician's exam are needed to know what is happening in this person.
urgent_if: Cannot move the leg or bear weight
Visible deformity or bone sticking out
Leg is pale, cold or numb
Severe pain not relieved by rest

about.reply: Leg injuries and disorders are problems with the bones, blood vessels, muscles and connective tissue in your legs that affect motion and standing. They are commonly caused by sports, running, falls or accidents, and by diseases such as knee osteoarthritis or vein problems like varicose veins and deep vein thrombosis.
about.next_step: See a doctor promptly for new leg pain after an injury, pain that limits walking, swelling, redness or warmth, or pain that does not improve in a few days.
about.why: Injuries like sprains, strains, dislocations and fractures can affect the whole leg or just the foot, ankle, knee or hip, and some leg problems come from long-term disease rather than a single injury.

care.reply: Measles is a very contagious viral illness that causes fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes and a blotchy red rash that often starts on the head and moves down the body. At home, keep the person isolated from others, especially babies, pregnant people and anyone not vaccinated, and focus on rest, fluids and fever comfort measures as advised by a clinician.
care.next_step: Contact a doctor today for advice on confirming the illness, isolation precautions and care at home, and do not go to a clinic without calling first.
care.why: Measles spreads easily by air and can lead to serious complications. A clinician can guide safe home care and when in-person care is needed, and the report's own range and their doctor's plan come first.
urgent_if: trouble breathing or fast breathing
not drinking and signs of dehydration
seizure or confusion
eye pain or vision changes

about.reply: Measles is an infectious viral illness that spreads very easily from person to person and causes fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes and a blotchy red rash that usually starts on the head and moves down the body.
about.next_step: See a doctor promptly if you or someone you care for develops fever with cough, runny nose, red eyes and a spreading rash, or tiny white spots inside the mouth.
about.why: It is caused by a measles virus and can lead to serious complications. The MMR vaccine can prevent it, and there is no specific treatment, so care is supportive and to prevent spread.

care.reply: Memory changes are common and can be normal with age, but new or worsening forgetfulness should be checked. Keep a simple daily routine, write things down, and note when the memory problems started and what is affected.
care.next_step: See a health care provider soon for an assessment, and seek care sooner if forgetfulness is getting worse or interfering with daily life.
care.why: Short-term memory stores information for seconds to minutes and long-term memory stores it longer. Forgetting names or keys can be normal, but forgetting how to use a phone or find the way home may signal a more serious problem.

about.reply: Memory is how your brain stores information and then recalls it later, with short-term memory holding things for seconds to minutes and long-term memory holding them for longer.
about.why: The brain decides what to keep, and forgetting occasionally is normal, especially with age. More frequent forgetting than peers, or losing skills like using a phone or finding your way home, can signal a more serious problem.

care.reply: Meningitis is inflammation of the membranes around the brain and spinal cord and can get serious very quickly. If someone at home has possible signs, get medical care right away today rather than waiting.
care.next_step: Take the person for urgent in-person medical evaluation now, and call 112 if they are very drowsy, confused, have trouble breathing, a seizure, or cannot be woken.
care.why: Bacterial meningitis can be deadly and can cause stroke, hearing loss and brain damage, and early treatment can help prevent serious problems. Viral meningitis is more common but still needs prompt assessment to confirm the cause.
urgent_if: Sudden high fever
Severe headache with stiff neck
Nausea or vomiting with confusion
Drowsiness, trouble waking, seizure or trouble breathing

about.reply: Meningitis is inflammation of the thin tissue that covers the brain and spinal cord, called the meninges. The most common type is viral, from a virus that enters through the nose or mouth; bacterial meningitis is rarer but can be deadly and is often caused by pneumococcal or meningococcal infections. Get medical care right away for sudden high fever, severe headache, stiff neck, or nausea or vomiting.
about.why: Viral meningitis is most common, bacterial is rare but can progress very quickly and cause serious complications. Early treatment can help prevent serious problems including death.

care.reply: Mouth problems can make eating, drinking, speaking and smiling hard. In general, keep the mouth clean and healthy by gentle brushing, flossing and not using tobacco, and avoid irritants like very spicy or acidic foods until it feels better.
care.next_step: Have the person seen by a doctor within 2 to 3 days if the sore, patch or dryness is not improving, is getting worse, or is making eating or drinking difficult.
care.why: Mouth disorders have many causes such as cold sores, canker sores, thrush, leukoplakia and dry mouth, and treatment depends on the specific problem. Some problems improve with basic care, while others need medical treatment, especially if caused by another disease.

about.reply: Mouth disorders are problems that affect your mouth and make it hard to eat, drink, breathe, speak or smile. Common examples are cold sores, canker sores, thrush, leukoplakia, dry mouth, gum or tooth problems and bad breath, often linked to viruses, bacteria, yeast, medicines, tobacco use or another disease.
about.next_step: See a doctor if a sore, white patch or dryness lasts more than 1 to 2 weeks, is getting worse, makes eating or drinking painful, or you notice bleeding gums, loose teeth or persistent bad breath.
about.why: The mouth helps take in food and drink, start digestion, breathe, speak and show emotion, so problems there can affect daily life. Treatment depends on the specific problem and keeping the mouth clean with brushing, flossing and avoiding tobacco helps.

care.reply: Mumps is caused by a virus and usually gets better on its own in about 7 to 10 days. At home the usual care is rest, fluids and gentle care for the swollen, tender salivary glands under the ears or jaw, and avoid close contact with others until the person is no longer contagious.
care.next_step: Keep the person at home, resting and drinking fluids, and avoid contact with others especially pregnant people, newborns and anyone not vaccinated, for about 5 days after swelling starts; check with a doctor today for advice on isolation and care.
care.why: There is no specific treatment for mumps and complications are rare, but it spreads by being with an infected person. The report’s own range and a doctor’s plan come first for individual care.
urgent_if: cannot drink or signs of dehydration
severe headache, neck stiffness or confusion
severe pain in testicles or breast area
trouble breathing or persistent high fever

about.reply: Mumps is an illness caused by the mumps virus that starts with fever, headache, muscle aches, tiredness and loss of appetite, and then often causes swollen, tender salivary glands under the ears or jaw on one or both sides. It spreads by close contact with someone who has it, and there is no specific treatment, but the measles-mumps-rubella vaccine can prevent it.
about.next_step: See a doctor if swelling of the glands develops, fever lasts more than a few days, or you are unsure about care and prevention.
about.why: Symptoms usually last 7 to 10 days and serious complications are rare, but a clinician can confirm the cause, advise on rest and symptom care, and check vaccination status.

care.reply: Nail health can reflect overall health, and healthy nails are usually smooth and consistent in color. For now keep nails clean, dry and trimmed, and do not remove the cuticle because that can allow infection.
care.next_step: If you notice pain, redness, swelling, thickening, discoloration that is spreading, drainage, an ingrown nail, or a nail change that is new and not improving, have a doctor look at it within 2 to 3 days.
care.why: Keeping nails clean and dry helps prevent bacterial and fungal problems, and cuticle removal can open the way for infection. Nail changes can sometimes be linked to lung, heart, kidney, liver diseases, diabetes and anemia, so a clinician can check the nail and the person’s overall health when needed.

about.reply: Nail diseases are problems with your fingernails or toenails that can change their color, shape, thickness or growth. Nails are made of keratin and their health can reflect overall health, with changes sometimes linked to lung, heart, kidney, liver diseases, diabetes and anemia.
about.next_step: See a doctor within 2 to 3 days if a nail is painful, red, swollen, thickened, crumbling, discolored, growing abnormally, or if you have an ingrown nail that is not improving with gentle care.
about.why: Keeping nails clean, dry and trimmed helps avoid problems, and not removing the cuticle reduces infection risk. The report notes specific discoloration and growth changes can be signs of systemic conditions, so persistent changes should be checked.

about.reply: Nutritional support is therapy to give nourishment when you cannot get enough by eating or drinking, usually through a vein with a needle or catheter or through a feeding tube into the stomach.
about.next_step: Talk to a doctor within 2 to 3 days if you or someone you care for cannot swallow safely, has a very poor appetite, is losing weight fast, or is severely malnourished.
about.why: It is used when swallowing problems, poor appetite, severe malnutrition, or poor nutrient absorption make normal eating unsafe or insufficient. The exact cause and the right type of support can only be decided by a doctor after examination.

care.reply: Pink eye is inflammation of the outer eye and eyelid that can cause redness, itching, burning, swelling and discharge. It can be infectious from bacteria or virus, allergic, or from irritation, and infectious pink eye can spread easily from person to person.
care.next_step: Keep hands clean, avoid touching or rubbing the eyes, do not share towels or pillowcases, and wash hands often. If symptoms are mild, they often improve with gentle care, but get a doctor seen within 1 to 2 days for advice on care and to check if antibiotic eye drops are needed.
care.why: Infectious pink eye spreads by contact and usually clears on its own, but bacterial pink eye often needs antibiotic eye drops or ointment. The report's own range and a doctor's plan come first for this person.
urgent_if: eye pain or vision changes
swelling that closes the eye
fever with eye redness
not improving after a few days

about.reply: Pink eye is the common name for conjunctivitis, which is inflammation of the thin outer layer of the eye and the inside of the eyelid. It commonly causes redness, swelling, itching, burning and discharge, and is often caused by bacterial or viral infection, allergies, or irritation from substances, contact lens products, eye drops or ointments. Infectious pink eye can spread easily from person to person.
about.next_step: See a doctor within 2 to 3 days if redness, discharge or irritation is not improving, if you have eye pain, vision changes, or if you wear contact lenses.
about.why: The evidence describes conjunctivitis as inflammation with those symptoms and those common causes. Bacterial pink eye usually needs antibiotic eye drops or ointment, while many cases clear on their own, so a clinician decides if treatment is needed.

care.reply: Premenstrual syndrome is a group of physical and emotional symptoms that often start one to two weeks before a period and usually go away after the period starts. For now, gentle self-care such as regular sleep, balanced meals, light movement and tracking symptoms day by day can help you see patterns.
care.next_step: Track symptoms for 2 to 3 cycles and see a doctor within 2 to 3 days if symptoms are severe, interfere with work or relationships, or are new and worrying.
care.why: Hormone changes during the menstrual cycle may play a role, and symptoms vary a lot between people and over time. Severe symptoms that interfere with life can be a more severe form like PMDD and need medical review.

about.reply: Premenstrual syndrome, or PMS, is a group of physical and emotional symptoms that usually start one to two weeks before your period and go away after your period starts. Most women have some symptoms, ranging from mild to severe.
about.why: PMS is linked to changing hormone levels during the menstrual cycle, though the exact cause is not known and these changes may affect women differently.

care.reply: Prostate diseases are not one single problem. The prostate is a gland below the bladder that makes fluid for semen, and common problems include prostatitis which is inflammation or infection of the prostate, benign enlargement of the prostate with age that can press on the urethra, and prostate cancer. Each has different causes and needs a doctor’s exam and tests to tell them apart.
care.next_step: Have the person see a doctor soon for a proper history, exam and tests, and do not start or stop any medicine on your own.
care.why: The symptoms and management differ a lot between prostatitis, enlarged prostate and prostate cancer, and only a clinician who can examine the person and order tests can say which is relevant and what care is needed.
urgent_if: fever with chills and pain in the lower belly or groin
sudden inability to pass urine or very little urine
blood in urine or semen
pain with urination with fever

about.reply: The prostate is a small gland below the bladder in men that makes fluid for semen. Prostate diseases are common problems of this gland, such as inflammation called prostatitis, age-related enlargement called BPH, and prostate cancer.
about.next_step: See a doctor within 2 to 3 days if you have new urinary problems, pelvic pain, fever with urinary symptoms, or blood in urine or semen.
about.why: Prostatitis is the most common prostate problem under age 50 and can be acute bacterial, chronic bacterial or chronic pelvic pain syndrome. Enlarged prostate is very common with age and can press on the urethra, while prostate cancer is common in men aged 50 and older.

care.reply: For a shoulder injury at home, start with general first aid and protect the shoulder while you watch for warning signs. The usual first step is RICE: Rest the shoulder, Ice for 15-20 minutes at a time with a cloth barrier, Compression with a light wrap if comfortable, and Elevation to help swelling.
care.next_step: Have the person seen a doctor within 2 to 3 days if pain, swelling or limited movement persists, or sooner if there was a fall, a direct hit, or the shoulder looks deformed.
care.why: The shoulder is very mobile but unstable, so muscles, tendons and ligaments can be injured easily. RICE is commonly used first for shoulder problems, but a history, exam and imaging are needed to know the cause.
urgent_if: shoulder looks deformed or visibly out of place
severe pain with inability to move the arm
numbness, tingling or pale/cold hand
fever with increasing redness and warmth

about.reply: Shoulder injuries and disorders are problems with the shoulder joint made of the collarbone, shoulder blade and upper arm bone, which is very movable but unstable and held in place by muscles, tendons and ligaments. Common problems include sprains and strains, dislocations, separations, tendinitis, bursitis, torn rotator cuff, frozen shoulder, fractures and arthritis. They often happen from falls, lifting, sports or repetitive overhead use, and first treatment is usually rest, ice, compression and elevation with pain relief and exercises.
about.next_step: See a doctor within 2 to 3 days if pain or limited movement is not improving with rest and ice, or sooner if you cannot lift the arm, have a visible deformity, or pain after a fall.
about.why: The shoulder ball is larger than its socket so it relies on soft tissues for stability, which makes it easy to injure. Diagnosis is by history, exam and imaging, and surgery is only considered if conservative care does not help.

care.reply: Sickle cell disease is an inherited red blood cell disorder where abnormal hemoglobin makes red cells stiff and sickle-shaped, which can break early and block small blood vessels. This can lead to anemia and sudden pain crises when oxygen does not reach tissues. It is a lifelong condition that needs regular medical follow-up and a plan for daily care.
care.next_step: Make sure the person has a regular doctor for sickle cell care and knows their personal action plan for pain and fever, and review it within the next few days if it is not already documented.
