care.why: Sickle cells last only 10 to 20 days instead of 90 to 120 days and can stick to vessel walls, causing low red cells and blockages that trigger pain crises. The exact triggers and best care vary by person, so a doctor’s plan comes first.
urgent_if: sudden severe pain crisis
fever 38.5°C or higher
trouble breathing or chest pain
confusion or drowsiness

about.reply: Sickle cell disease is an inherited red blood cell disorder where abnormal hemoglobin makes red cells stiff and sickle-shaped instead of flexible discs. The sickle cells break apart early and can block small blood vessels, which can lead to anemia and sudden severe pain crises.
about.why: It is caused by an inherited gene variant that changes how hemoglobin is made, as described in the evidence. The sickle shape makes cells less flexible and short-lived, which can reduce oxygen delivery.

care.reply: Skin infections happen when germs enter through a break in the skin or in moist areas where skin rubs, and they can stay on the surface or go deeper. Keep the area clean and dry, avoid picking or squeezing it, and do not share towels or clothes. Cover small wounds with a clean dry dressing and wash hands before and after touching the area.
care.next_step: Have a clinician look at the skin today if there is spreading redness, warmth, swelling, pus, fever, red streaks up the limb, or if the person has diabetes, poor circulation or a weakened immune system; otherwise book a check within 2 to 3 days for any new or worsening skin infec
care.why: Germs can enter through cuts or moist skin and infections can spread under the skin or to the bloodstream, especially in people with diabetes, poor circulation or a weakened immune system. The exact cause and needed care depend on the type of infection and the person’s health.
urgent_if: Fever with spreading redness or warmth
Rapidly spreading redness or red streaks up the limb
Blistering, black skin or severe pain
Confusion, drowsiness or feeling very unwell

about.reply: A skin infection is when germs get into the skin through a break, cut or wound, or in moist areas where skin rubs, and grow there. It is commonly caused by bacteria such as staph and strep, and also by viruses, fungi and parasites.
about.why: Your skin normally keeps germs out, but breaks in the skin, poor blood supply, diabetes or a weakened immune system make infection more likely. The type of germ determines the kind of infection, and infections can stay on the surface or go deeper and spread.

about.reply: Smoking is inhaling tobacco smoke, usually from cigarettes, which contains nicotine and many harmful chemicals. People often start because of peer influence, stress, curiosity or family habits, and nicotine quickly causes addiction.
about.next_step: If you smoke and want to quit, or you have cough, chest tightness, shortness of breath, or repeated infections, talk to a doctor within the next few days for support and check-up.
about.why: Nicotine is addictive and smoke harms nearly every organ, increasing risk of cancer, lung and heart disease. The exact reasons someone starts vary, and health risks build over time.

care.reply: Snoring is common and often happens when airway tissues vibrate during sleep, and it can be reduced by sleeping on the side, avoiding alcohol and sedatives at bedtime, and keeping a regular sleep routine. See a doctor if snoring is loud and frequent, causes daytime tiredness or poor sleep, or is linked to gasping or choking at night.
care.next_step: Try side sleeping and avoid alcohol or sedatives at bedtime tonight, and note how often snoring happens and any daytime sleepiness for the next few days.
care.why: Weight, sleep position and alcohol can worsen snoring, and severe snoring can be a sign of sleep apnea which needs medical assessment. The report's own range and doctor's plan come first for any test.
urgent_if: waking up gasping or choking
cannot breathe during sleep
sudden confusion or very sleepy during the day

about.reply: Snoring is a sound made when breathing is partly blocked during sleep, causing tissues at the top of your airway to vibrate. It is common in older people and people who are overweight, and can be made worse by sleeping on your back or having alcohol or sedatives at bedtime.
about.why: The sound comes from vibrating airway tissues when airflow is narrowed. Thin people can snore too, and severe snoring can disrupt sleep and be a sign of sleep apnea.

care.reply: Get the person out of the sun now into shade or indoors, and cool the skin gently with cool water and loose clothing while offering fluids if they can drink safely.
care.next_step: Keep them out of direct sun for the rest of the day and check the skin in the next 24 hours for blistering, pain or worsening redness; see a doctor today if blisters form, skin peels a lot, or they feel very unwell.
care.why: UV rays can damage skin cells even without a burn and damage can happen in any season. Protection and early cooling reduce further damage, but the report’s own range and a doctor’s plan come first for personal care.
urgent_if: confusion or drowsiness
trouble breathing
not responding
very high fever with hot dry skin

about.reply: Sun exposure is damage to your skin and eyes from ultraviolet UV rays from the sun, which you cannot see. It commonly happens when you are outside in sunlight, especially between 10 a.m. and 2 p.m., and also from sunlamps and tanning beds.
about.why: UV rays pass through skin and can damage skin cells, causing sunburn, tanning, wrinkles, spots and skin cancer. Damage can occur in any season or temperature.

care.reply: Call 112 now. Tetanus is a medical emergency and needs hospital treatment right away, do not wait at home.
care.next_step: Call 112 now and get the person to hospital immediately. Do not give food or medicine by mouth.
care.why: It can only be managed in hospital with supportive care and tetanus-specific treatment.
urgent_if: jaw locking or cannot open mouth
painful muscle stiffness all over the body
trouble swallowing or breathing
recent deep cut, puncture wound or burn

about.reply: Tetanus is a serious infection caused by Clostridium bacteria that live in soil, dust, saliva and manure. It usually enters through a deep cut, like stepping on a nail, or a burn, and causes painful muscle tightening and can lock the jaw so you cannot open your mouth or swallow.
about.next_step: If you have a deep cut, puncture wound or burn, see a doctor today for wound care and to check if a tetanus booster is needed.
about.why: The bacteria release a toxin that affects nerves and muscles. A vaccine and prompt wound care can prevent infection, and adults need a booster every 10 years.

care.reply: Thalassemia is an inherited blood disorder where the body makes fewer healthy red blood cells and less hemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen. This can cause anemia, and severity ranges from mild with no or few symptoms to severe with marked anemia, slowed growth and organ problems.
care.next_step: Have the person evaluated by a doctor now for confirmation and a care plan, and follow the doctor’s advice for regular blood tests and monitoring.
care.why: Diagnosis is made with blood tests and management depends on severity, from no treatment for mild forms to transfusions, iron removal and specialist care for severe forms. The exact plan can only be set by a clinician who has examined the person.
urgent_if: pale skin with severe tiredness or shortness of breath
chest pain or pressure
rapid breathing or trouble breathing
confusion or fainting

about.reply: Thalassemia is an inherited blood disorder where the body makes fewer healthy red blood cells and less hemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen, which leads to anemia.
about.why: It is inherited, so it runs in families and is more common in people of Italian, Greek, Middle Eastern, Southern Asian and African descent. Severity ranges from mild or no symptoms to severe anemia with growth, spleen, liver, heart or bone problems.

care.reply: Tinnitus is ringing, roaring, clicking, hissing or buzzing in one or both ears and it can be soft or loud. It is common and often linked to hearing changes, loud noise exposure, ear or sinus issues, blood vessel problems, certain medicines and thyroid changes. Now keep the home quiet, avoid loud noise and very loud music, and note when it started, if it is in one or both ears and any medicines being used.
care.next_step: Book a check with a doctor within 2 to 3 days if the ringing is new, persistent, or affecting sleep or work, and sooner if it came on suddenly with hearing loss.
care.why: Treatment depends on the cause, and a clinician can check hearing and look for treatable contributors. The evidence describes tinnitus sounds and common causes but does not tell which cause applies to this person.
urgent_if: sudden loss of hearing in one ear
severe dizziness or trouble walking
severe headache with tinnitus
fever with ear pain and swelling

about.reply: Tinnitus is the perception of ringing, buzzing, hissing, roaring or clicking sounds in one or both ears when no external sound is present.
about.why: It is common and often linked to hearing loss with age, loud noise exposure, ear and sinus infections, heart or blood vessel problems, Meniere's disease, thyroid problems, hormonal changes and certain medicines. Treatment depends on the cause and may include hearing aids, sound-masking devices, medicines and coping strategies.

care.reply: Tonsillitis is swelling of the tonsils, usually from a viral infection and sometimes from bacteria like strep. At home, rest, warm fluids, and gentle salt-water gargles can help comfort, and pain relief can be used as per the label or prescription. Keep hands clean to reduce spread of the germs that cause it.
care.next_step: See a doctor today if there is trouble swallowing, signs of dehydration, breathing difficulty, a high fever that does not come down, or if symptoms are not improving after 3 to 4 days.
care.why: Viral tonsillitis often improves with supportive care, but bacterial causes may need specific treatment and complications can occur. The report's own range and a clinician's exam decide if testing or medicine is needed.
urgent_if: trouble breathing or noisy breathing
cannot swallow fluids or signs of dehydration
very high fever with confusion or drowsiness
severe one-sided throat swelling

about.reply: Tonsillitis is swelling and inflammation of the tonsils, the two lumps of tissue at the back of your throat that help trap germs. It is most commonly caused by a viral infection, and sometimes by bacterial infections such as strep throat.
about.next_step: See a doctor within 2 to 3 days if sore throat is severe, swallowing is difficult, fever lasts more than 3 days, or you are not improving with rest and fluids.
about.why: Tonsils are part of the lymphatic system and trap germs from mouth and nose. Viruses cause most cases, especially in younger children, while bacterial tonsillitis is more common in kids ages 5 to 15.

care.reply: Urinary incontinence is loss of bladder control and can range from mild leakage to a big impact on daily life. It can improve with proper treatment, and a clinician can find the type and causes and suggest safe ways to manage it.
care.next_step: Book a check with a doctor within the next 2 to 3 days for assessment and advice, and keep a simple note of when leaks happen, triggers and fluid intake until the visit.
care.why: There are different types such as stress, urge and overflow incontinence with different causes, and some causes like a urinary tract infection or bladder not emptying need medical care. The report's own range and the doctor's plan come first.
urgent_if: fever with burning or pain on passing urine
blood in urine
sudden inability to pass urine with lower belly pain
confusion or drowsiness in an older person

about.reply: Urinary incontinence is loss of bladder control and leaking urine when you cannot hold it. It can be mild or greatly affect daily life, and it can often get better with proper treatment.
about.next_step: Talk to a doctor if leakage happens regularly, is bothersome, or you notice a strong sudden urge with leaking, especially if you have fever, burning with urination, or pain.
about.why: It has several types with different causes, such as stress on the bladder from coughing or weak pelvic floor muscles, and urge incontinence linked to an overactive bladder or sometimes a urinary tract infection.

care.reply: Urine is made by the kidneys and stored in the bladder, which can comfortably hold about 16 ounces for 2 to 5 hours before you need to urinate. Many different things can change urination, such as infection, bladder control problems, prostate enlargement, blockage or kidney problems, and a doctor can check with urinalysis and other urine tests.
care.next_step: Note what is different, such as pain, burning, blood in urine, inability to pass urine, leaking, or fever, and book a check with a health care provider within the next 2 to 3 days for new or ongoing urinary changes.
care.why: The urinary system filters waste from blood and stores urine until you urinate. Because many conditions can cause similar urinary changes, a clinician needs to examine the person and test the urine to find the cause and decide treatment.
urgent_if: cannot pass urine at all or severe lower belly pain
fever with back pain or burning urination
visible blood in urine with clots
confusion or drowsiness with urinary symptoms

about.reply: Urine is waste, mainly urea, that your kidneys filter from blood and store in the bladder until you urinate. The bladder can comfortably hold about 16 ounces for 2 to 5 hours before you need to empty it.
about.why: Kidneys make urine by filtering wastes and extra water, and it travels via ureters to the bladder which swells when full and shrinks when empty. Problems with urination can happen when the urinary system is not working normally.

care.reply: Uterine fibroids are common noncancerous growths in the uterus that often cause no symptoms and can be monitored with a doctor's guidance.
care.next_step: Book a check-up with a doctor soon for an exam and history, and sooner if there are heavy periods, pelvic pain or pressure, or pregnancy concerns.
care.why: Fibroids vary in size and number and many women have no problems, but some can cause heavy bleeding, pain, fertility or pregnancy issues. Only a clinician who can examine the person can decide what monitoring or care is needed.

about.reply: Uterine fibroids are noncancerous, benign growths made of muscle and other tissue that develop in or around the wall of the uterus. Many people have them and never know it because they often cause no symptoms, and they can be single or multiple and vary in size.
about.next_step: Talk to a doctor if you have heavy or prolonged periods, pelvic pressure or pain, trouble getting pregnant, pregnancy loss, or any new pelvic symptoms that worry you.
about.why: Fibroids are common in women of childbearing age and risk is higher with older age, Black/African American ethnicity, family history, early period start before age 10, never being pregnant, obesity and vitamin D deficiency. Risk lowers with pregnancy and long-term use of birth control pills or shots.

care.reply: Varicose veins are swollen, twisted veins, often in the legs, that happen when vein valves are weak and blood pools. At home, gentle movement, leg elevation when resting, avoiding long standing and tight clothing can help keep them from getting worse.
care.next_step: Book a check with a doctor within 2 to 3 days if the veins are painful, changing in colour, or you are unsure, and sooner if there are new symptoms.
care.why: Exercise, weight management and leg elevation reduce pooling in the veins. A doctor can confirm the diagnosis by exam and discuss options if they are painful or bothersome.
urgent_if: sudden leg swelling with pain and warmth
skin ulcer or bleeding from a vein
severe pain or rapid change in leg colour

about.reply: Varicose veins are swollen, twisted veins you can see just under the skin, most often in the legs. They happen when one-way valves in veins weaken and blood pools back up, making the veins swell.
about.why: Weak or damaged valves let blood flow backward and pool, which stretches the veins. Risk is higher with age, female sex, obesity, little exercise, family history, pregnancy and long periods of standing.

care.reply: Vital signs are basic measurements of how your body is working, including blood pressure, heart rate or pulse, breathing rate, and temperature. They are usually checked at a doctor's office or during an emergency visit to spot problems early.
care.next_step: If you are worried about someone at home, note any symptoms they have and have their vital signs checked by a doctor within the next few days for a proper checkup.
care.why: Blood pressure, heart rate, breathing and temperature can be too high or too low and cause problems, and normal ranges depend on age, activity, medicines and other factors. The report's own ranges and a clinician's assessment come first.
urgent_if: not breathing normally
chest pain or pressure
sudden confusion or fainting
very high fever or trouble breathing

about.reply: Vital signs are basic measurements of how your body is functioning, usually checked at a doctor's visit. They are blood pressure, heart rate or pulse, respiratory rate or breathing rate, and temperature.
about.why: These four signs are used to monitor heart, breathing and body temperature. Changes can come from exercise, stress, fever, illness, medicines or age, and the normal range depends on the person.

care.reply: Warts are skin growths caused by human papilloma virus, HPV. In children they often go away on their own, while in adults they tend to stay, and they can be removed if they hurt, bother you or multiply.
care.next_step: If the wart is painful, bleeding, changing quickly, multiplying, or you are unsure what it is, book a check with a doctor within 2 to 3 days. For genital warts, see a doctor promptly.
care.why: HPV causes different types of warts such as common, plantar, flat and genital. Removal options exist, but the right choice depends on the type, location and the person’s health, so a clinician should decide.

about.reply: Warts are small skin growths caused by infection with human papilloma virus, or HPV. They can appear as common warts on fingers, plantar warts on the soles of feet, flat warts in shaved areas, and genital warts which are a sexually transmitted infection.
about.why: HPV infects the outer skin layer and causes extra skin to grow. In children warts often go away on their own, but in adults they tend to stay.

care.reply: Weight loss surgery is a medical procedure for extreme obesity when diet and exercise are not enough or obesity is causing serious health problems. It limits how much food you can eat and in some types changes digestion and nutrient absorption, and it needs lifelong medical follow-up.
care.next_step: If someone at home has had weight loss surgery, ask their doctor today about the lifelong follow-up plan for diet, exercise, nutrient checks and warning signs.
care.why: All types have risks such as infection, hernia and blood clots, and weight can be regained without ongoing care. The report's own plan and their doctor's advice come first.

about.reply: Weight loss surgery is an operation that helps people with extreme obesity lose weight by limiting how much food you can eat and sometimes changing how food is digested and absorbed.
about.why: It is considered when diet and exercise are not enough or obesity is causing serious health problems. All types have risks like infection, hernia and blood clots and need lifelong medical follow-up.

care.reply: Zika is spread mainly by mosquitoes and can also pass from a pregnant mother to her baby and through sexual contact. Most people have no symptoms, and when symptoms occur they are usually mild fever, rash, joint pain and red eyes starting 2 to 7 days after a bite. Care at home is rest, drinking lots of fluids and avoiding mosquito bites so you do not spread it to others.
care.next_step: Get medical advice today for testing and guidance, and urgently if the person is pregnant or could be pregnant, or if symptoms worsen.
care.why: There is no vaccine or specific medicine for Zika, and a blood test can tell if the infection is present. The main risks are for pregnancy, which is why doctor advice is needed promptly.

about.reply: Zika is a virus spread mostly by mosquito bites, and it can also pass from a pregnant mother to her baby and through sexual contact. Most people have no symptoms, but about one in five get mild fever, rash, joint pain and red eyes 2 to 7 days after a bite. There is no vaccine or specific medicine; care is fluids, rest and acetaminophen as advised by a doctor.
about.next_step: Talk to your doctor before travel if you are pregnant or planning pregnancy, and seek care promptly if you develop fever, rash, joint pain or red eyes after possible exposure.
about.why: Mosquito bites are the common cause, and infection in pregnancy can cause serious brain problems in babies. Symptoms are usually mild but need medical advice to confirm and to protect pregnancy.
